AS tenant_id, tenant_counts.haproxy_lb_count AS tenant_haproxy_loadbalancer_count, avg_counts.avg_haproxy_lb_count AS avg_haproxy_loadbalancers_per_tenant FROM inner_cte JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb ON lb.NAME = inner_cte.loadbalancer_name AND lb.VIP_ADDRESS = inner_cte.vip_address JOIN ( SELECT lb2.TENANT_ID, COUNT(lb2.ID) AS haproxy_lb_count FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb2 JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra2 ON lb2.ID = pra2.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra2.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' GROUP BY lb2.TENANT_ID ) AS tenant_counts ON tenant_counts.TENANT_ID = lb.TENANT_ID JOIN ( SELECT AVG(sub.haproxy_lb_count) AS avg_haproxy_lb_count FROM ( SELECT lb3.TENANT_ID, COUNT(lb3.ID) AS haproxy_lb_count FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb3 JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra3 ON lb3.ID = pra3.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra3.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' GROUP BY lb3.TENANT_ID ) AS sub ) AS avg_counts ON 1 = 1 ) SELECT q1.TENANT_ID, q1.total_online_haproxy_loadbalancers, q1.overall_online_haproxy_loadbalancers, q2.loadbalancer_name, q2.vip_address, q2.bytes_in, q2.total_connections, q2.window_column, q2.tenant_haproxy_loadbalancer_count, q2.avg_haproxy_loadbalancers_per_tenant FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q2.tenant_id = q1.TENANT_ID ORDER BY q1.total_online_haproxy_loadbalancers DESC, q2.loadbalancer_name;

question: For the top 10 port statuses with the highest coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of ports’ standard attribute IDs (considering only ports that have both a security group port binding and a port security binding), show the port status, the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP), whether any of those ports have a floating IP allocated, and how many of the top 10 tenants (ranked by the highest coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of allocated IP address string lengths for ports with port security enabled) have ports in that same status. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH subq1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ) SELECT i.status, i.coefficient_of_variation, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT f.id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_floating_ips FROM inner_cte i JOIN ports p ON p.status = i.status JOIN securitygroupportbindings sgpb ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN floatingips f ON f.fixed_port_id = p.id GROUP BY i.status, i.coefficient_of_variation ORDER BY i.coefficient_of_variation DESC LIMIT 10 ), subq2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.status, STDDEV(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) / NULLIF(AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM portsecuritybindings psb JOIN ports p ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON p.id = ia.port_id WHERE psb.port_security_enabled = 1 GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC) SELECT p.tenant_id, STDDEV(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) / NULLIF(AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)), 0) AS tenant_coefficient_of_variation, CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN p.status = 'ACTIVE' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_active_ports, CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN p.status = 'DOWN' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_down_ports, CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN p.status = 'BUILD' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_build_ports FROM portsecuritybindings psb JOIN ports p ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON p.id = ia.port_id JOIN inner_cte ic ON ic.status = p.status WHERE psb.port_security_enabled = 1 GROUP BY p.tenant_id HAVING AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) > 0 ORDER BY tenant_coefficient_of_variation DESC LIMIT 10 ) SELECT s1.status, s1.coefficient_of_variation, s1.has_floating_ips, COUNT(DISTINCT s2.tenant_id) AS top_tenants_with_ports_in_that_status FROM subq1 s1 JOIN ports p ON p.status = s1.status JOIN subq2 s2 ON s2.tenant_id = p.tenant_id GROUP BY s1.status, s1.coefficient_of_variation, s1.has_floating_ips ORDER BY s1.coefficient_of_variation DESC;

question: For each tenant that (1) has ports in status 'DOWN' with port security enabled and (2) has at least one port bound to a security group with admin_state_up = 1, list the tenant ID, the total number of down-and-secure ports and the average down-and-secure port count across all tenants, along with the tenant’s total number of admin-up ports with security group bindings, the total security group bindings and DNS records across those ports, and the average number of such admin-up ports per tenant. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH down_secure_ports_by_tenant AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 ) SELECT p.tenant_id AS ports_tenant_id, COUNT(p.id) AS total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled, avg_counts.avg_down_secure_port_count FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id JOIN ( SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_down_secure_port_count FROM ( SELECT p2.tenant_id, COUNT(p2.id) AS port_count FROM ports p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings psb2 ON p2.id = psb2.port_id WHERE p2.status = 'DOWN' AND psb2.port_security_enabled = 1 GROUP BY p2.tenant_id ) AS sub ) AS avg_counts ON 1 = 1 CROSS JOIN inner_cte WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND psb.port_security_enabled = 1 GROUP BY p.tenant_id, avg_counts.avg_down_secure_port_count ), sg_admin_up_ports_by_tenant AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name) SELECT inner_cte.tenant_id, COUNT(inner_cte.port_id) AS total_ports_with_sg_binding_admin_up, SUM(inner_cte.security_group_binding_count) AS total_security_group_bindings, SUM(inner_cte.dns_record_count) AS total_dns_records, avg_ports.avg_port_count AS avg_ports_with_sg_binding_admin_up_per_tenant FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count FROM ( SELECT COUNT(port_id) AS port_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS sub ) AS avg_ports GROUP BY inner_cte.tenant_id, avg_ports.avg_port_count ) SELECT ds.ports_tenant_id AS tenant_id, ds.total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled, ds.avg_down_secure_port_count, sa.total_ports_with_sg_binding_admin_up, sa.total_security_group_bindings, sa.total_dns_records, sa.avg_ports_with_sg_binding_admin_up_per_tenant FROM down_secure_ports_by_tenant ds JOIN sg_admin_up_ports_by_tenant sa ON sa.tenant_id = ds.ports_tenant_id;

question: For each tenant that has at least one ACTIVE network, show the tenant ID, the latest standard-attribute updated_at timestamp across that tenant’s active networks, the number of ports (that are admin_state_up = 1 and bound to a security group), the average security-group binding count per such port, the total number of DNS records across those ports, and the average deviation of each port’s security-group binding count from the overall average binding count. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH port_sg_dns_deviation AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(security_group_binding_count) AS avg_sg_binding_count FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.port_name, i.security_group_binding_count, i.dns_record_count, (i.security_group_binding_count - a.avg_sg_binding_count) AS deviation_from_avg_sg_binding_count FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a ), tenant_active_network_latest_update AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT tenant_id, MAX(standard_attr_updated_at) AS latest_standard_attr_updated_at FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) SELECT psdd.tenant_id, tanlu.latest_standard_attr_updated_at, COUNT(DISTINCT psdd.port_id) AS port_count, AVG(psdd.security_group_binding_count) AS avg_security_group_binding_count_per_port, SUM(psdd.dns_record_count) AS total_dns_record_count_across_ports, AVG(psdd.deviation_from_avg_sg_binding_count) AS avg_deviation_from_avg_sg_binding_count FROM port_sg_dns_deviation psdd JOIN tenant_active_network_latest_update tanlu ON psdd.tenant_id = tanlu.tenant_id GROUP BY psdd.tenant_id, tanlu.latest_standard_attr_updated_at ORDER BY port_count DESC;

question: For ports whose status is 'DOWN', list each port’s tenant ID, port ID, port name, MAC address, allocated IP address, and subnet ID, along with (1) the average port ID within each port-ID group ordered by IP address, (2) the total number of allocated IPs in that subnet and how far that subnet’s allocation count deviates from the average across all subnets, and (3) the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within its security group plus the security group’s total DOWN-port count and its deviation from the average DOWN-port count across all security groups, ordered by IP address. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ia.SUBNET_ID AS subnet_id, AVG(p.ID) OVER (PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ), SubnetAllocations AS ( SELECT ia.subnet_id, COUNT(DISTINCT ia.ip_address) AS allocated_ips FROM IPALLOCATIONS ia GROUP BY ia.subnet_id ), AverageAllocations AS ( SELECT AVG(allocated_ips) AS avg_ips FROM SubnetAllocations ) SELECT i.port_id, i.port_name, i.mac_address, i.ip_address, i.subnet_id, i.window_column, sa.allocated_ips AS subnet_allocated_ips, (sa.allocated_ips - aa.avg_ips) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i JOIN SubnetAllocations sa ON i.subnet_id = sa.subnet_id CROSS JOIN AverageAllocations aa ORDER BY i.ip_address ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), SecurityGroupDownCounts AS ( SELECT sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS security_group_id, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_in_group FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ), AverageDownCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_ports_in_group) AS avg_down_ports_in_group FROM SecurityGroupDownCounts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.window_column, sgdc.down_ports_in_group, (sgdc.down_ports_in_group - adc.avg_down_ports_in_group) AS deviation_from_avg_down_ports FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb ON sgpb.PORT_ID = i.port_id JOIN SecurityGroupDownCounts AS sgdc ON sgdc.security_group_id = sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID CROSS JOIN AverageDownCounts AS adc ) SELECT q2.tenant_id, q1.port_id, q1.port_name, q1.mac_address, q1.ip_address, q1.subnet_id, q1.window_column AS avg_port_id_within_port_id_group_by_ip, q1.subnet_allocated_ips, q1.deviation_from_avg AS subnet_allocations_deviation_from_avg, q2.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_security_group, q2.down_ports_in_group, q2.deviation_from_avg_down_ports FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q1.port_id = q2.port_id ORDER BY q1.ip_address;

question: For IPv4 subnets whose max_standard_attr_id_next2 (the maximum subnet standard attribute ID over the current subnet row and the next 2 rows when ordered by subnet ID) is greater than the average max_standard_attr_id_next2 for subnets with the same DHCP-enabled flag, list only those subnets that belong to a network that is in the top 3 most-subnetted networks shared via RBAC action 'access_as_shared' and whose subnet count is above the average subnet count of those top 3 networks; return the network ID, tenant ID, subnet name, IP version, CIDR, gateway IP, DHCP enabled flag, allocation pool first/last IP, max_standard_attr_id_next2, the shared network’s subnet count, and the number of distinct target tenants it is shared with. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH SubnetDetails AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ), DhcpAverages AS ( SELECT ENABLE_DHCP, AVG(max_standard_attr_id_next2) AS avg_max_next2 FROM inner_cte GROUP BY ENABLE_DHCP ) SELECT i.NAME, i.TENANT_ID, i.NETWORK_ID, i.IP_VERSION, i.CIDR, i.GATEWAY_IP, i.ENABLE_DHCP, i.FIRST_IP, i.LAST_IP, i.max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM inner_cte i JOIN DhcpAverages d ON i.ENABLE_DHCP = d.ENABLE_DHCP WHERE i.max_standard_attr_id_next2 > d.avg_max_next2 ), TopSharedNetworks AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.OBJECT_ID AS network_id, COUNT(*) AS subnet_count FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.OBJECT_ID ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 3), AvgTop3 AS ( SELECT AVG(subnet_count) AS avg_subnet_count FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.network_id, i.subnet_count, COUNT(DISTINCT r.TARGET_TENANT) AS distinct_target_tenants FROM inner_cte i JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON r.OBJECT_ID = i.network_id AND r.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY i.network_id, i.subnet_count HAVING i.subnet_count > (SELECT avg_subnet_count FROM AvgTop3) ORDER BY i.subnet_count DESC ), CombinedResults AS ( SELECT sd.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, sd.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, sd.NAME AS subnet_name, sd.IP_VERSION AS ip_version, sd.CIDR AS cidr, sd.GATEWAY_IP AS gateway_ip, sd.ENABLE_DHCP AS enable_dhcp, sd.FIRST_IP AS first_ip, sd.LAST_IP AS last_ip, sd.max_standard_attr_id_next2 AS max_standard_attr_id_next2, tsn.subnet_count AS shared_network_subnet_count, tsn.distinct_target_tenants AS shared_network_distinct_target_tenants FROM SubnetDetails sd JOIN TopSharedNetworks tsn ON tsn.network_id = sd.NETWORK_ID ) SELECT * FROM CombinedResults ORDER BY network_id, subnet_name;

question: For ports bound to security group ID 0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c, find only those ports whose standard attribute ID is greater than the average standard attribute ID of all ports in the same network. For these filtered ports, return the port ID, port status, allocated IP address, the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within each network (ordered by standard attribute ID), and also include the owning tenant ID, that tenant’s total number of ports in this security group, and the average of these per-tenant totals across all tenants. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH HighStdAttrPortsInNetwork AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.STATUS AS port_status, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c') SELECT inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.port_status, inner_cte.ip_address, inner_cte.window_column FROM inner_cte JOIN PORTS p2 ON p2.ID = inner_cte.port_id WHERE p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID > (SELECT AVG(p3.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) FROM PORTS p3 WHERE p3.NETWORK_ID = p2.NETWORK_ID)), TenantPortStatsInSG AS (WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.STATUS AS port_status, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' ) SELECT inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.port_status, inner_cte.ip_address, inner_cte.window_column, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, COUNT(p.ID) AS total_ports_for_tenant_in_sg, avg_ports.avg_port_count AS avg_ports_per_tenant_in_sg FROM inner_cte JOIN PORTS p ON inner_cte.port_id = p.ID JOIN ( SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count FROM ( SELECT COUNT(p2.ID) AS port_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb2 JOIN PORTS p2 ON sgpb2.PORT_ID = p2.ID WHERE sgpb2.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' GROUP BY p2.TENANT_ID ) AS sub ) AS avg_ports ON 1 = 1 GROUP BY inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.port_status, inner_cte.ip_address, inner_cte.window_column, p.TENANT_ID, avg_ports.avg_port_count) SELECT tps.port_id, tps.port_status, tps.ip_address, tps.window_column, tps.tenant_id, tps.total_ports_for_tenant_in_sg, tps.avg_ports_per_tenant_in_sg FROM TenantPortStatsInSG tps WHERE tps.port_id IN (SELECT port_id FROM HighStdAttrPortsInNetwork) ORDER BY tps.tenant_id, tps.port_id;

question: For allowed address pairs on port ID `25d421c1-c76d-4c26-9550-9f871a1d5034`, list each allowed MAC and IP along with the port ID and its bound security group ID, the running average of the port’s standard attribute ID (partitioned by port and ordered by allowed IP) and its deviation from the overall average running average; also include, for that same security group, the range/variance/standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of allowed-address-pair counts per port (counting only ports that have at least one allowed address pair), the overall average range benchmark, and the security group’s spread category (HIGH_SPREAD/LOW_SPREAD/AVERAGE_SPREAD). Do not return any rounded answers. Categorize each security group as 'HIGH_SPREAD' (at least 50% above the benchmark), 'LOW_SPREAD' (at least 50% below the benchmark), or 'AVERAGE_SPREAD'.
SQL: WITH sg_spread_stats AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MAX(port_pair_count) - MIN(port_pair_count) AS pair_count_range, VARIANCE(port_pair_count) AS pair_count_variance, STDDEV(port_pair_count) AS pair_count_stddev FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS port_pair_count FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ALLOWEDADDRESSPAIRS AS aap ON p.ID = aap.PORT_ID GROUP BY p.ID ) AS port_stats ON sgpb.PORT_ID = port_stats.port_id GROUP BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY pair_count_range DESC ), AverageRange AS ( SELECT AVG(pair_count_range) AS avg_pair_count_range FROM inner_cte ) SELECT ic.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, ic.pair_count_range, ic.pair_count_variance, ic.pair_count_stddev, ar.avg_pair_count_range AS benchmark, CASE WHEN ic.pair_count_range > ar.avg_pair_count_range * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_SPREAD' WHEN ic.pair_count_range < ar.avg_pair_count_range * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_SPREAD' ELSE 'AVERAGE_SPREAD' END AS spread_category FROM inner_cte ic CROSS JOIN AverageRange ar ), port_25d421c1_allowed_pairs AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT aap.MAC_ADDRESS AS allowed_mac_address, aap.IP_ADDRESS AS allowed_ip_address, p.ID AS port_id, sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS security_group_id, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY aap.IP_ADDRESS ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN ALLOWEDADDRESSPAIRS AS aap ON p.ID = aap.PORT_ID WHERE p.ID = '25d421c1-c76d-4c26-9550-9f871a1d5034' ORDER BY aap.IP_ADDRESS ), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(window_column) AS avg_window_column FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.allowed_mac_address, i.allowed_ip_address, i.port_id, i.security_group_id, i.window_column, (i.window_column - a.avg_window_column) AS deviation_from_avg_window FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a ORDER BY i.allowed_ip_address ) SELECT p.allowed_mac_address, p.allowed_ip_address, p.port_id, p.security_group_id, p.window_column, p.deviation_from_avg_window, s.pair_count_range, s.pair_count_variance, s.pair_count_stddev, s.benchmark AS avg_pair_count_range_benchmark, s.spread_category FROM port_25d421c1_allowed_pairs p JOIN sg_spread_stats s ON s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = p.security_group_id ORDER BY p.allowed_ip_address;

question: For ports that are in status 'DOWN', list each port’s tenant ID and port ID along with its host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and the row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row). Also show, per host, the total number of DOWN-port IP allocations and each row’s deviation from the average host total, and for the same tenant include the tenant’s count of DOWN ports with port security enabled, the overall average of that count across tenants as a benchmark, the tenant’s user category (HIGH_USER/LOW_USER/AVERAGE_USER), and the overall total number of DOWN ports with port security enabled. Do not return any rounded answers. Classify each tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), HostCounts AS ( SELECT host, COUNT(DISTINCT ip_address) AS down_allocated_ips FROM inner_cte GROUP BY host ), AverageHostCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_allocated_ips) AS avg_down_allocated_ips FROM HostCounts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.window_column, hc.down_allocated_ips, (hc.down_allocated_ips - ahc.avg_down_allocated_ips) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i JOIN HostCounts hc ON i.host = hc.host CROSS JOIN AverageHostCounts ahc ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 ), TenantDownSecurePorts AS ( SELECT p.TENANT_ID, COUNT(*) AS down_secure_ports FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 GROUP BY p.TENANT_ID ), AverageDownSecurePorts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_secure_ports) AS avg_down_secure_ports FROM TenantDownSecurePorts ) SELECT tdsp.TENANT_ID, tdsp.down_secure_ports, adsp.avg_down_secure_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tdsp.down_secure_ports > adsp.avg_down_secure_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tdsp.down_secure_ports < adsp.avg_down_secure_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category, inner_cte.down_ports_with_port_security_enabled AS overall_down_secure_ports FROM TenantDownSecurePorts tdsp CROSS JOIN AverageDownSecurePorts adsp CROSS JOIN inner_cte ) SELECT q1.tenant_id, q2.user_category, q2.down_secure_ports, q2.benchmark AS avg_down_secure_ports_benchmark, q2.overall_down_secure_ports, q1.port_id, q1.host, q1.vif_type, q1.ip_address, q1.window_column, q1.down_allocated_ips, q1.deviation_from_avg FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q1.tenant_id = q2.TENANT_ID ORDER BY q2.user_category, q1.tenant_id, q1.ip_address;

question: For ports that are in status 'DOWN', list each port’s ID, tenant ID, and MAC address, along with the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within its security group (ordered by standard attribute ID). Also show the total number of DOWN ports in that security group and how far that group’s DOWN-port count deviates from the average DOWN-port count across all security groups; additionally, for the same tenant, include how many DOWN ports have port security enabled, that tenant’s deviation from the average tenant count, and the overall total number of DOWN ports with port security enabled. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), SecurityGroupDownCounts AS ( SELECT sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS security_group_id, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_in_group FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ), AverageDownCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_ports_in_group) AS avg_down_ports_in_group FROM SecurityGroupDownCounts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.window_column, sgdc.down_ports_in_group, (sgdc.down_ports_in_group - adc.avg_down_ports_in_group) AS deviation_from_avg_down_ports FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb ON sgpb.PORT_ID = i.port_id JOIN SecurityGroupDownCounts AS sgdc ON sgdc.security_group_id = sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID CROSS JOIN AverageDownCounts AS adc ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1), TenantDownSecurePorts AS (SELECT p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS down_secure_ports FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 GROUP BY p.TENANT_ID), AverageTenantCounts AS (SELECT AVG(down_secure_ports) AS avg_down_secure_ports FROM TenantDownSecurePorts) SELECT tdsp.tenant_id, tdsp.down_secure_ports, (tdsp.down_secure_ports - atc.avg_down_secure_ports) AS deviation_from_avg, inner_cte.down_ports_with_port_security_enabled AS total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM TenantDownSecurePorts tdsp CROSS JOIN AverageTenantCounts atc CROSS JOIN inner_cte ) SELECT q1.port_id, q1.tenant_id, q1.mac_address, q1.window_column, q1.down_ports_in_group, q1.deviation_from_avg_down_ports, q2.down_secure_ports, q2.deviation_from_avg, q2.total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q2.tenant_id = q1.tenant_id;

question: For each RBAC action (plus a final TOTAL row), show the standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of subnet IP versions for DHCP-enabled subnets on the RBAC-referenced networks (only actions with more than 5 such subnets), together with the IPv4-only subnet IP-version average/variance/standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) and the total number of distinct IPv4 subnets involved for that same action. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.ACTION, STDDEV(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_stddev FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.ENABLE_DHCP = 1 GROUP BY n.ACTION HAVING COUNT(*) > 5 ORDER BY ip_version_stddev DESC ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(action) OVER (ORDER BY action_sort, action) = action THEN NULL ELSE action END AS action, ip_version_stddev FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.action) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE i.action END AS action_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.action) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE i.action END AS action, STDDEV(i.ip_version_stddev) AS ip_version_stddev FROM inner_cte i GROUP BY i.action WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY action_sort ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.ACTION, AVG(s.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance, STDDEV(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_stddev FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_variance DESC ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(action) OVER (ORDER BY action_sort, action) = action THEN NULL ELSE action END AS action, avg_ip_version, ip_version_variance, ip_version_stddev, distinct_subnets FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.action) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE i.action END AS action_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.action) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE i.action END AS action, MAX(i.avg_ip_version) AS avg_ip_version, MAX(i.ip_version_variance) AS ip_version_variance, MAX(i.ip_version_stddev) AS ip_version_stddev, COUNT(DISTINCT s.id) AS distinct_subnets FROM inner_cte i JOIN NETWORKRBACS n ON n.action = i.action JOIN SUBNETS s ON s.network_id = n.object_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY i.action WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY action_sort, action ) SELECT COALESCE(q1.action, q2.action) AS action, q1.ip_version_stddev AS dhcp_enabled_ip_version_stddev_over_actions, q2.avg_ip_version AS ipv4_avg_ip_version, q2.ip_version_variance AS ipv4_ip_version_variance, q2.ip_version_stddev AS ipv4_ip_version_stddev, q2.distinct_subnets AS ipv4_distinct_subnets FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q2.action = q1.action OR (q2.action = 'TOTAL' AND q1.action = 'TOTAL');

question: For the top 10 IPv4 subnets with the largest route-count range, list each subnet’s name, route-count range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP), along with the subnet tenant ID and whether DHCP is enabled, and also show the details of the ACTIVE network that subnet belongs to (network name, status, admin_state_up, RBAC action, RBAC target tenant with its dense-rank value, and the network MTU plus its deviation from the average MTU across all ACTIVE networks). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH SubnetRouteRangeStats AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(route_count) - MIN(route_count) AS route_count_range, VARIANCE(route_count) AS route_count_variance, STDDEV(route_count) AS route_count_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN ( SELECT sr.SUBNET_ID, COUNT(*) AS route_count FROM SUBNETROUTES AS sr GROUP BY sr.SUBNET_ID, sr.NEXTHOP ) AS route_stats ON s.ID = route_stats.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY route_count_range DESC ) SELECT inner_cte.subnet_name, inner_cte.route_count_range, inner_cte.route_count_variance, inner_cte.route_count_stddev, s.tenant_id, CASE WHEN s.enable_dhcp = 1 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS dhcp_enabled FROM inner_cte JOIN subnets s ON s.name = inner_cte.subnet_name WHERE s.ip_version = 4 ORDER BY inner_cte.route_count_range DESC LIMIT 10 ), ActiveNetworkRbacAndMtuStats AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.name, n.status, n.admin_state_up, r.action, r.target_tenant, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY n.id ORDER BY n.id) AS window_column FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE'), ActiveNetworkMTU AS ( SELECT n.id AS network_id, n.mtu FROM networks n WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' ), AverageActiveMTU AS ( SELECT AVG(mtu) AS avg_mtu FROM ActiveNetworkMTU ) SELECT i.name, i.status, i.admin_state_up, i.action, i.target_tenant, i.window_column, anm.mtu, (anm.mtu - aam.avg_mtu) AS deviation_from_avg_mtu FROM inner_cte i JOIN networks n ON n.name = i.name AND n.status = i.status AND n.admin_state_up = i.admin_state_up JOIN ActiveNetworkMTU anm ON anm.network_id = n.id CROSS JOIN AverageActiveMTU aam ) SELECT srrs.subnet_name, srrs.route_count_range, srrs.route_count_variance, srrs.route_count_stddev, srrs.tenant_id AS subnet_tenant_id, srrs.dhcp_enabled, anrms.name AS network_name, anrms.status AS network_status, anrms.admin_state_up, anrms.action AS rbac_action, anrms.target_tenant AS rbac_target_tenant, anrms.window_column AS rbac_dense_rank_within_network, anrms.mtu AS network_mtu, anrms.deviation_from_avg_mtu FROM SubnetRouteRangeStats srrs JOIN subnets s ON s.name = srrs.subnet_name AND s.ip_version = 4 JOIN ActiveNetworkRbacAndMtuStats anrms ON anrms.status = 'ACTIVE' JOIN networkrbacs r ON r.action = anrms.action AND r.target_tenant = anrms.target_tenant JOIN networks n ON n.id = r.object_id AND n.name = anrms.name AND n.status = anrms.status AND n.admin_state_up = anrms.admin_state_up JOIN subnets s2 ON s2.network_id = n.id AND s2.ip_version = 4 AND s2.name = srrs.subnet_name ORDER BY srrs.route_count_range DESC, anrms.deviation_from_avg_mtu DESC;

question: For each port status and admin-state category (including subtotals and the grand total) among ports with port security enabled, show the status, whether the port is Admin Up or Admin Down, the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of allocated IP address string lengths, and—only for the DOWN status—the number of distinct DOWN ports that appear in the security-group DOWN-port listing. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(security_group_id) OVER (ORDER BY security_group_id_sort, security_group_id, port_id) = security_group_id THEN NULL ELSE security_group_id END AS security_group_id, port_id, tenant_id, mac_address, window_column, down_ports_in_group FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.security_group_id) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE i.security_group_id END AS security_group_id_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.security_group_id) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE i.security_group_id END AS security_group_id, i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.window_column, COUNT(i.port_id) AS down_ports_in_group FROM inner_cte i GROUP BY i.security_group_id, i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.window_column WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY security_group_id_sort, security_group_id, port_id ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.status, STDDEV(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) / NULLIF(AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM portsecuritybindings psb JOIN ports p ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON p.id = ia.port_id WHERE psb.port_security_enabled = 1 GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC), PortStatusAdmin AS ( SELECT p.status, CASE WHEN p.admin_state_up = 1 THEN 'Admin Up' ELSE 'Admin Down' END AS admin_state, STDDEV(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) / NULLIF(AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM portsecuritybindings psb JOIN ports p ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON p.id = ia.port_id JOIN inner_cte ic ON ic.status = p.status WHERE psb.port_security_enabled = 1 GROUP BY p.status, admin_state HAVING AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) > 0 ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(status) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE status END AS status, CASE WHEN GROUPING(admin_state) = 1 AND GROUPING(status) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE admin_state END AS admin_state, AVG(coefficient_of_variation) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM PortStatusAdmin GROUP BY status, admin_state WITH ROLLUP ) SELECT q2.status, q2.admin_state, q2.coefficient_of_variation, COUNT(DISTINCT q1.port_id) AS down_ports_with_security_group_rows FROM q2 LEFT JOIN q1 ON q2.status = 'DOWN' GROUP BY q2.status, q2.admin_state, q2.coefficient_of_variation ORDER BY q2.status, q2.admin_state;

question: For ACTIVE networks whose total number of RBAC entries is greater than the average RBAC-entry count across all ACTIVE networks, return the network name, status, and admin_state_up along with each RBAC action and target tenant, the number of distinct RBAC target tenants per network, and the dense-rank value within each network (partitioned by network ID and ordered by network ID). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS (WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.name, n.status, n.admin_state_up, r.action, r.target_tenant, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY n.id ORDER BY n.id) AS window_column FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' ), NetworkRbacCounts AS ( SELECT n.id AS network_id, COUNT(r.id) AS total_rbacs FROM networks n JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n.id ) SELECT i.name, i.status, i.admin_state_up, i.action, i.target_tenant, i.window_column FROM inner_cte i JOIN networks n ON n.name = i.name AND n.status = i.status AND n.admin_state_up = i.admin_state_up JOIN NetworkRbacCounts c ON c.network_id = n.id WHERE c.total_rbacs > (SELECT AVG(total_rbacs) FROM NetworkRbacCounts)), q2 AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.name, n.status, n.admin_state_up, r.action, r.target_tenant, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY n.id ORDER BY n.id) AS window_column FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE'), rbac_counts AS ( SELECT n.id AS network_id, COUNT(DISTINCT r.target_tenant) AS distinct_target_tenants FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n.id ) SELECT i.name, i.status, i.admin_state_up, i.action, i.target_tenant, c.distinct_target_tenants, i.window_column FROM inner_cte i JOIN rbac_counts c ON c.network_id = (SELECT n2.id FROM networks n2 WHERE n2.name = i.name AND n2.status = i.status AND n2.admin_state_up = i.admin_state_up LIMIT 1)) SELECT q1.name, q1.status, q1.admin_state_up, q1.action, q1.target_tenant, q2.distinct_target_tenants, q1.window_column FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q1.name = q2.name AND q1.status = q2.status AND q1.admin_state_up = q2.admin_state_up AND q1.action = q2.action AND q1.target_tenant = q2.target_tenant AND q1.window_column = q2.window_column;

question: For networks that are ACTIVE, list each network’s ID, name, tenant ID, admin_state_up flag, MTU, and standard attribute updated_at timestamp (with a row number within each tenant ordered by network name), along with the benchmark average MTU across all active networks and an MTU category (ABOVE_AVG_MTU/BELOW_AVG_MTU/AT_AVG_MTU); for those same networks, also list any ports that are DOWN on the network including port ID, tenant ID, port name, MAC address, device owner, allocated IP address, the row number within each network ordered by port ID, the total number of DOWN port IP allocations on that network, and that total’s deviation from the average across all networks. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH down_ports AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), NetworkDownAllocations AS ( SELECT network_id, COUNT(DISTINCT ip_address) AS down_allocated_ips FROM inner_cte GROUP BY network_id ), AverageNetworkDownAllocations AS ( SELECT AVG(down_allocated_ips) AS avg_down_allocated_ips FROM NetworkDownAllocations ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.port_name, i.network_id, i.mac_address, i.device_owner, i.ip_address, i.window_column, nda.down_allocated_ips, (nda.down_allocated_ips - anda.avg_down_allocated_ips) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i JOIN NetworkDownAllocations nda ON i.network_id = nda.network_id CROSS JOIN AverageNetworkDownAllocations anda ), active_networks AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE'), AvgMtu AS (SELECT AVG(mtu) AS avg_mtu FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.network_id, i.network_name, i.tenant_id, i.admin_state_up, i.mtu, i.standard_attr_updated_at, i.window_column, a.avg_mtu AS benchmark_avg_mtu, CASE WHEN i.mtu > a.avg_mtu THEN 'ABOVE_AVG_MTU' WHEN i.mtu < a.avg_mtu THEN 'BELOW_AVG_MTU' ELSE 'AT_AVG_MTU' END AS mtu_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN AvgMtu a ) SELECT an.network_id, an.network_name, an.tenant_id AS network_tenant_id, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at, an.window_column AS network_row_number_within_tenant, an.benchmark_avg_mtu, an.mtu_category, dp.port_id, dp.tenant_id AS port_tenant_id, dp.port_name, dp.mac_address, dp.device_owner, dp.ip_address, dp.window_column AS port_row_number_within_network, dp.down_allocated_ips, dp.deviation_from_avg AS deviation_from_avg_down_allocated_ips FROM active_networks an JOIN down_ports dp ON dp.network_id = an.network_id;

question: For port statuses that (1) have an average STANDARD_ATTR_ID above the overall average among ports bound with VIF type 'ovs' and (2) also appear among DOWN ports that are bound to a security group, list the port status, device owner (including the subtotal row per status), distinct port count, minimum standard attribute ID, and the corresponding minimum ADMIN_STATE_UP and average STANDARD_ATTR_ID from the 'ovs' bound ports for that same status. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH ovs_status_stats AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) AS min_admin_state_up, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS avg_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE b.VIF_TYPE = 'ovs' GROUP BY p.STATUS) SELECT p.STATUS, inner_cte.min_admin_state_up, inner_cte.avg_standard_attr_id FROM inner_cte JOIN PORTS p ON 1 = 1 JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE b.VIF_TYPE = 'ovs' GROUP BY p.STATUS, inner_cte.min_admin_state_up, inner_cte.avg_standard_attr_id HAVING inner_cte.avg_standard_attr_id > (SELECT AVG(p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) FROM PORTS p2 JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b2 ON p2.ID = b2.PORT_ID WHERE b2.VIF_TYPE = 'ovs') ), down_sg_rollup AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(port_status) OVER (ORDER BY port_status_sort, port_status, device_owner) = port_status THEN NULL ELSE port_status END AS port_status, device_owner, port_count, min_standard_attr_id FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(port_status) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE port_status END AS port_status_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(device_owner) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE device_owner END AS device_owner, port_status, SUM(port_count) AS port_count, MIN(min_standard_attr_id) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM inner_cte GROUP BY port_status, device_owner WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY port_status_sort, port_status, device_owner ) SELECT dsr.port_status, dsr.device_owner, dsr.port_count, dsr.min_standard_attr_id, oss.min_admin_state_up, oss.avg_standard_attr_id FROM down_sg_rollup dsr JOIN ovs_status_stats oss ON dsr.port_status = oss.STATUS WHERE dsr.port_status IS NOT NULL;

question: For tenants that have at least 1 port on host "drive-59", list their DOWN ports (port ID, tenant ID, port name, network ID, MAC address, device owner, allocated IP address, and the row number within each network ordered by port ID), along with each port’s network-level total number of DOWN allocated IPs and that total’s deviation from the average across networks; also show, per tenant, the total number of distinct ports on "drive-59" and whether the tenant has any ports with port security enabled. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH down_ports AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), NetworkDownAllocations AS ( SELECT network_id, COUNT(DISTINCT ip_address) AS down_allocated_ips FROM inner_cte GROUP BY network_id ), AverageNetworkDownAllocations AS ( SELECT AVG(down_allocated_ips) AS avg_down_allocated_ips FROM NetworkDownAllocations ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.port_name, i.network_id, i.mac_address, i.device_owner, i.ip_address, i.window_column, nda.down_allocated_ips, (nda.down_allocated_ips - anda.avg_down_allocated_ips) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i JOIN NetworkDownAllocations nda ON i.network_id = nda.network_id CROSS JOIN AverageNetworkDownAllocations anda ), drive59_tenants AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' ) SELECT i.TENANT_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT i.PORT_ID) AS total_ports, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT psb.PORT_ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_port_security_enabled FROM inner_cte AS i LEFT JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON i.PORT_ID = psb.PORT_ID GROUP BY i.TENANT_ID ORDER BY total_ports DESC ) SELECT dp.port_id, dp.tenant_id, dp.port_name, dp.network_id, dp.mac_address, dp.device_owner, dp.ip_address, dp.window_column, dp.down_allocated_ips, dp.deviation_from_avg, dt.total_ports AS drive59_total_ports_for_tenant, dt.has_port_security_enabled FROM down_ports dp JOIN drive59_tenants dt ON dp.tenant_id = dt.tenant_id WHERE dp.tenant_id IS NOT NULL AND dt.total_ports >= 1 ORDER BY dt.total_ports DESC, dp.network_id, dp.window_column;

question: For the top 10 port binding hosts with the highest variance in port standard attribute ID (considering only ports that are DOWN and have an IP allocation), list each host’s variance, total number of distinct DOWN ports with IP allocations, and whether any of those ports belong to a tenant that has any port in the system; for each of those hosts, also show the detailed DOWN port records on that host including port ID, tenant ID, port name, network ID, MAC address, device owner, allocated IP address, the row number within each network ordered by port ID, the total number of DOWN port IP allocations per network, and that network’s deviation from the average DOWN allocations across all networks. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH down_ports_by_network AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), NetworkDownAllocations AS ( SELECT network_id, COUNT(DISTINCT ip_address) AS down_allocated_ips FROM inner_cte GROUP BY network_id ), AverageNetworkDownAllocations AS ( SELECT AVG(down_allocated_ips) AS avg_down_allocated_ips FROM NetworkDownAllocations ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.port_name, i.network_id, i.mac_address, i.device_owner, i.ip_address, i.window_column, nda.down_allocated_ips, (nda.down_allocated_ips - anda.avg_down_allocated_ips) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i JOIN NetworkDownAllocations nda ON i.network_id = nda.network_id CROSS JOIN AverageNetworkDownAllocations anda), top_hosts_by_variance AS (WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT b.HOST, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND ia.PORT_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY b.HOST ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ) SELECT i.HOST, i.standard_attr_id_variance, COUNT(DISTINCT p2.ID) AS total_down_ports_with_ip, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT p3.ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS tenant_has_any_ports FROM inner_cte i JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b2 ON i.HOST = b2.HOST JOIN PORTS p2 ON b2.PORT_ID = p2.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia2 ON p2.ID = ia2.PORT_ID LEFT JOIN PORTS p3 ON p3.TENANT_ID = p2.TENANT_ID WHERE p2.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND ia2.PORT_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY i.HOST, i.standard_attr_id_variance ORDER BY i.standard_attr_id_variance DESC LIMIT 10), down_ports_with_hosts AS ( SELECT dpbn.port_id, dpbn.tenant_id, dpbn.port_name, dpbn.network_id, dpbn.mac_address, dpbn.device_owner, dpbn.ip_address, dpbn.window_column, dpbn.down_allocated_ips, dpbn.deviation_from_avg, b.HOST FROM down_ports_by_network dpbn JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON b.PORT_ID = dpbn.port_id ) SELECT dph.HOST, thbv.standard_attr_id_variance, thbv.total_down_ports_with_ip, thbv.tenant_has_any_ports, dph.port_id, dph.tenant_id, dph.port_name, dph.network_id, dph.mac_address, dph.device_owner, dph.ip_address, dph.window_column, dph.down_allocated_ips, dph.deviation_from_avg FROM down_ports_with_hosts dph JOIN top_hosts_by_variance thbv ON dph.HOST = thbv.HOST ORDER BY thbv.standard_attr_id_variance DESC, dph.HOST, dph.network_id, dph.window_column;

question: For each default external network (where IS_DEFAULT = 0), list the tenant and network details (network ID, name, status, admin state up, MTU, standard attribute ID), the minimum MTU within that tenant, the total number of such default external networks per tenant and the average of that total across tenants; and, for ports on each network whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports', also show the port status and device owner along with the number of ports, the earliest standard attribute updated timestamp, and the deviation of that port count from the overall average across all port status/owner groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH port_status_owner_stats AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER), avg_cte AS (SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.earliest_standard_attr_update, (i.port_count - a.avg_port_count) AS deviation_from_avg_port_count FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a ), default_external_networks_by_tenant AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT e.NETWORK_ID, e.IS_DEFAULT, n.TENANT_ID, n.NAME, n.STATUS, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP, n.MTU, n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID, MIN(n.MTU) OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.TENANT_ID) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0 ) SELECT inner_cte.NETWORK_ID, inner_cte.IS_DEFAULT, inner_cte.TENANT_ID, inner_cte.NAME, inner_cte.STATUS, inner_cte.ADMIN_STATE_UP, inner_cte.MTU, inner_cte.STANDARD_ATTR_ID, inner_cte.window_column, tenant_counts.total_default_external_networks, avg_counts.avg_default_external_networks_per_tenant FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT TENANT_ID, COUNT(NETWORK_ID) AS total_default_external_networks FROM inner_cte GROUP BY TENANT_ID ) AS tenant_counts ON inner_cte.TENANT_ID = tenant_counts.TENANT_ID JOIN ( SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_default_external_networks_per_tenant FROM ( SELECT COUNT(NETWORK_ID) AS cnt FROM inner_cte GROUP BY TENANT_ID ) AS sub ) AS avg_counts ON 1 = 1 ) SELECT den.TENANT_ID, den.NETWORK_ID, den.IS_DEFAULT, den.NAME AS network_name, den.STATUS AS network_status, den.ADMIN_STATE_UP, den.MTU, den.STANDARD_ATTR_ID AS network_standard_attr_id, den.window_column AS min_mtu_within_tenant, den.total_default_external_networks, den.avg_default_external_networks_per_tenant, pso.port_status, pso.device_owner, pso.port_count, pso.earliest_standard_attr_update, pso.deviation_from_avg_port_count FROM default_external_networks_by_tenant den LEFT JOIN PORTS p ON p.NETWORK_ID = den.NETWORK_ID LEFT JOIN port_status_owner_stats pso ON pso.port_status = p.STATUS AND pso.device_owner = p.DEVICE_OWNER ORDER BY den.TENANT_ID, den.NETWORK_ID, pso.port_count DESC;

question: For each port status that (among ports bound with VIF type 'ovs') has a minimum admin_state_up and an average standard_attr_id greater than the overall average standard_attr_id across all 'ovs'-bound ports, what are the status, that minimum admin_state_up, that average standard_attr_id, and (for the same status among ports that have both a security group port binding and a port security binding) the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of standard_attr_id and the total number of distinct security groups involved? Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) AS min_admin_state_up, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS avg_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE b.VIF_TYPE = 'ovs' GROUP BY p.STATUS) SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, inner_cte.min_admin_state_up, inner_cte.avg_standard_attr_id FROM inner_cte JOIN PORTS p ON p.STATUS = p.STATUS JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE b.VIF_TYPE = 'ovs' GROUP BY p.STATUS, inner_cte.min_admin_state_up, inner_cte.avg_standard_attr_id HAVING inner_cte.avg_standard_attr_id > ( SELECT AVG(p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) FROM PORTS p2 JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b2 ON p2.ID = b2.PORT_ID WHERE b2.VIF_TYPE = 'ovs' ) ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(status) OVER (ORDER BY status_sort, status) = status THEN NULL ELSE status END AS status, coefficient_of_variation, distinct_security_groups FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.status) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE i.status END AS status_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.status) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE i.status END AS status, AVG(i.coefficient_of_variation) AS coefficient_of_variation, COUNT(DISTINCT sgpb.security_group_id) AS distinct_security_groups FROM inner_cte i JOIN ports p ON p.status = i.status JOIN securitygroupportbindings sgpb ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id GROUP BY i.status WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY status_sort, status ) SELECT q1.port_status, q1.min_admin_state_up, q1.avg_standard_attr_id, q2.coefficient_of_variation, q2.distinct_security_groups FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q2.status = q1.port_status;

question: For ACTIVE networks that are shared via an RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', list the network name, status, admin_state_up, RBAC action, and RBAC target tenant (including the dense-rank value from the ACTIVE-network RBAC/MTU view), along with the network MTU and its deviation from the average MTU across all ACTIVE networks; also include each related shared subnet’s name and CIDR, the running sum of subnet standard attribute IDs within each IP-version group ordered by standard attribute ID, plus the total number of such shared subnets per RBAC target tenant and the average of those totals across all target tenants. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH shared_subnets AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER (PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ) SELECT i.subnet_name, i.subnet_cidr, i.rbac_target_tenant, i.window_column, tgt_counts.total_shared_subnets, avg_counts.avg_shared_subnets_per_target FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN ( SELECT rbac_target_tenant, COUNT(*) AS total_shared_subnets FROM inner_cte GROUP BY rbac_target_tenant ) AS tgt_counts ON tgt_counts.rbac_target_tenant = i.rbac_target_tenant JOIN ( SELECT AVG(total_shared_subnets) AS avg_shared_subnets_per_target FROM ( SELECT rbac_target_tenant, COUNT(*) AS total_shared_subnets FROM inner_cte GROUP BY rbac_target_tenant ) AS per_target ) AS avg_counts ), active_network_rbac_mtu AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.name, n.status, n.admin_state_up, r.action, r.target_tenant, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY n.id ORDER BY n.id) AS window_column FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE'), ActiveNetworkMTU AS ( SELECT n.id AS network_id, n.mtu FROM networks n WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' ), AverageActiveMTU AS ( SELECT AVG(mtu) AS avg_mtu FROM ActiveNetworkMTU ) SELECT i.name, i.status, i.admin_state_up, i.action, i.target_tenant, i.window_column, anm.mtu, (anm.mtu - aam.avg_mtu) AS deviation_from_avg_mtu FROM inner_cte i JOIN networks n ON n.name = i.name AND n.status = i.status AND n.admin_state_up = i.admin_state_up JOIN ActiveNetworkMTU anm ON anm.network_id = n.id CROSS JOIN AverageActiveMTU aam ), active_shared_networks AS ( SELECT n.id AS network_id, n.name AS network_name, n.status AS network_status, n.admin_state_up, r.action AS rbac_action, r.target_tenant AS rbac_target_tenant FROM networks n JOIN networkrbacs r ON r.object_id = n.id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' AND r.action = 'access_as_shared' ) SELECT asn.network_name, asn.network_status, asn.admin_state_up, asn.rbac_action, asn.rbac_target_tenant, anrm.window_column AS network_dense_rank_within_id, anrm.mtu, anrm.deviation_from_avg_mtu, ss.subnet_name, ss.subnet_cidr, ss.window_column AS running_sum_subnet_standard_attr_id_within_ip_version, ss.total_shared_subnets, ss.avg_shared_subnets_per_target FROM active_shared_networks asn JOIN active_network_rbac_mtu anrm ON anrm.name = asn.network_name AND anrm.status = asn.network_status AND anrm.admin_state_up = asn.admin_state_up AND anrm.action = asn.rbac_action AND anrm.target_tenant = asn.rbac_target_tenant JOIN networkrbacs r2 ON r2.object_id = asn.network_id AND r2.action = 'access_as_shared' AND r2.target_tenant = asn.rbac_target_tenant JOIN subnets s ON s.network_id = asn.network_id JOIN shared_subnets ss ON ss.subnet_name = s.name AND ss.subnet_cidr = s.cidr AND ss.rbac_target_tenant = asn.rbac_target_tenant ORDER BY asn.rbac_target_tenant, asn.network_name, ss.subnet_name;

question: For DOWN ports that belong to security groups whose count of DOWN ports is above the average across security groups, list each port’s ID, tenant ID, MAC address, security group ID, and its rank within that security group (ordered by port ID), along with the security group’s DOWN-port count; also include, for the same tenant, the tenant’s port-security rollup metrics for admin status = 'Up' (total ports, total port security bindings, and total times port security is enabled). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH down_ports_ranked AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN'), sg_counts AS ( SELECT security_group_id, COUNT(*) AS down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY security_group_id ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.security_group_id, i.window_column, c.down_ports FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN sg_counts AS c ON i.security_group_id = c.security_group_id WHERE c.down_ports > (SELECT AVG(down_ports) FROM sg_counts) ), tenant_admin_rollup AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ), TenantPortSecurityRollup AS ( SELECT p.tenant_id, CASE WHEN p.admin_state_up = 1 THEN 'Up' ELSE 'Down' END AS admin_status, COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS total_ports, COALESCE(SUM(inner_cte.binding_count), 0) AS total_bindings, COALESCE(SUM(inner_cte.port_security_enabled_total), 0) AS total_port_security_enabled FROM ports p LEFT JOIN inner_cte ON p.id = inner_cte.port_id GROUP BY p.tenant_id, admin_status ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(tenant_id) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE tenant_id END AS tenant_id, CASE WHEN GROUPING(admin_status) = 1 AND GROUPING(tenant_id) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' WHEN GROUPING(admin_status) = 1 AND GROUPING(tenant_id) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE admin_status END AS admin_status, SUM(total_ports) AS total_ports, SUM(total_bindings) AS total_bindings, SUM(total_port_security_enabled) AS total_port_security_enabled FROM TenantPortSecurityRollup GROUP BY tenant_id, admin_status WITH ROLLUP ) SELECT dpr.port_id, dpr.tenant_id, dpr.mac_address, dpr.security_group_id, dpr.window_column AS port_rank_within_security_group_by_port_id, dpr.down_ports AS down_ports_in_security_group, tar.admin_status, tar.total_ports, tar.total_bindings, tar.total_port_security_enabled FROM down_ports_ranked AS dpr JOIN tenant_admin_rollup AS tar ON dpr.tenant_id = tar.tenant_id WHERE tar.admin_status = 'Up';

question: For ports that are administratively up and also have status DOWN, list the port ID, tenant ID, and MAC address, along with (1) the number of port security bindings on the port, the total number of times port security is enabled across those bindings, and that enabled total’s deviation from the average enabled total across all administratively up ports, and (2) the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within its security group plus the security group’s total DOWN-port count and that count’s deviation from the average DOWN-port count across all security groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(port_security_enabled_total) AS avg_enabled_total FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.binding_count, i.port_security_enabled_total, (i.port_security_enabled_total - a.avg_enabled_total) AS deviation_from_avg_enabled_total FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), SecurityGroupDownCounts AS ( SELECT sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS security_group_id, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_in_group FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ), AverageDownCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_ports_in_group) AS avg_down_ports_in_group FROM SecurityGroupDownCounts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.window_column, sgdc.down_ports_in_group, (sgdc.down_ports_in_group - adc.avg_down_ports_in_group) AS deviation_from_avg_down_ports FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb ON sgpb.PORT_ID = i.port_id JOIN SecurityGroupDownCounts AS sgdc ON sgdc.security_group_id = sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID CROSS JOIN AverageDownCounts AS adc ) SELECT q1.port_id, q1.tenant_id, q1.mac_address, q1.binding_count, q1.port_security_enabled_total, q1.deviation_from_avg_enabled_total, q2.window_column, q2.down_ports_in_group, q2.deviation_from_avg_down_ports FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q1.port_id = q2.port_id AND q1.tenant_id = q2.tenant_id AND q1.mac_address = q2.mac_address;

question: On host "drive-59", how many distinct tenants have ports there, how many of those tenants are classified as HIGH_USER based on their count of DOWN ports with port security enabled versus the cross-tenant average benchmark, and how many of those tenants have any port security enabled (also report the overall total number of DOWN ports with port security enabled across all tenants)? Do not return any rounded answers. Classify each tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 ), TenantDownSecurePorts AS ( SELECT p.TENANT_ID, COUNT(*) AS down_secure_ports FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 GROUP BY p.TENANT_ID ), AverageDownSecurePorts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_secure_ports) AS avg_down_secure_ports FROM TenantDownSecurePorts ) SELECT tdsp.TENANT_ID, tdsp.down_secure_ports, adsp.avg_down_secure_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tdsp.down_secure_ports > adsp.avg_down_secure_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tdsp.down_secure_ports < adsp.avg_down_secure_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category, inner_cte.down_ports_with_port_security_enabled AS overall_down_secure_ports FROM TenantDownSecurePorts tdsp CROSS JOIN AverageDownSecurePorts adsp CROSS JOIN inner_cte ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' ) SELECT i.TENANT_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT i.PORT_ID) AS total_ports, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT psb.PORT_ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_port_security_enabled FROM inner_cte AS i LEFT JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON i.PORT_ID = psb.PORT_ID GROUP BY i.TENANT_ID ORDER BY total_ports DESC ) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT q2.TENANT_ID) AS tenants_on_drive_59, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN q1.user_category = 'HIGH_USER' THEN q2.TENANT_ID END) AS high_user_tenants_on_drive_59, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN q2.has_port_security_enabled = 'Yes' THEN q2.TENANT_ID END) AS tenants_on_drive_59_with_port_security_enabled, MAX(q1.overall_down_secure_ports) AS overall_down_secure_ports FROM q2 JOIN q1 ON q2.TENANT_ID = q1.TENANT_ID;

question: For ports that are both (a) bound to a security group with admin_state_up = 1 and (b) in status DOWN, list the port ID, tenant ID, port name, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and the row number ordered by IP address (with a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row), along with the port’s security group binding count, total DNS record count, deviation of its security group binding count from the average across all admin_state_up = 1 security-group-bound ports, and (for that tenant) the total number of DOWN ports plus the average DOWN-port count across all tenants. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH sg_dns_stats AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(security_group_binding_count) AS avg_sg_binding_count FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.port_name, i.security_group_binding_count, i.dns_record_count, (i.security_group_binding_count - a.avg_sg_binding_count) AS deviation_from_avg_sg_binding_count FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a), down_port_details AS (WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.tenant_id, inner_cte.host, inner_cte.vif_type, inner_cte.ip_address, inner_cte.window_column, tenant_counts.total_down_ports, avg_down.avg_down_port_count FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(port_id) AS total_down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS tenant_counts ON inner_cte.tenant_id = tenant_counts.tenant_id JOIN ( SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_port_count FROM ( SELECT COUNT(port_id) AS down_port_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS sub ) AS avg_down ON 1 = 1) SELECT d.port_id, d.tenant_id, s.port_name, d.host, d.vif_type, d.ip_address, d.window_column, s.security_group_binding_count, s.dns_record_count, s.deviation_from_avg_sg_binding_count, d.total_down_ports, d.avg_down_port_count FROM down_port_details d JOIN sg_dns_stats s ON d.port_id = s.port_id WHERE s.tenant_id = d.tenant_id;

question: For tenants classified as HIGH_USER based on having at least 50% more DOWN ports than the average tenant, list each DOWN port’s port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and its row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row). Also include the tenant’s total DOWN ports, the average DOWN-port benchmark, and—when available for the same port—the MAC address plus the port’s IP-allocation count and subnet-id row count from administratively up ports with IP allocations, along with the tenant’s total number of administratively up ports that have at least one IP allocation (restricted to tenants/ports with status DOWN). Do not return any rounded answers. Classify the tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'.
SQL: WITH down_ports AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), TenantDownPorts AS ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT port_id) AS total_down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ), AverageDownPorts AS ( SELECT AVG(total_down_ports) AS avg_down_ports FROM TenantDownPorts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.window_column, tdp.total_down_ports, adp.avg_down_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tdp.total_down_ports > adp.avg_down_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tdp.total_down_ports < adp.avg_down_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM inner_cte i JOIN TenantDownPorts tdp ON i.tenant_id = tdp.tenant_id CROSS JOIN AverageDownPorts adp), admin_up_ipalloc_rollup AS (WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ia.subnet_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS subnet_id_rows FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(tenant_id) OVER (ORDER BY tenant_id_sort, tenant_id, port_id) = tenant_id THEN NULL ELSE tenant_id END AS tenant_id, port_id, mac_address, ip_allocation_count, subnet_id_rows FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(inner_cte.tenant_id) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE inner_cte.tenant_id END AS tenant_id_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(inner_cte.tenant_id) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE inner_cte.tenant_id END AS tenant_id, CASE WHEN GROUPING(inner_cte.port_id) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE inner_cte.port_id END AS port_id, CASE WHEN GROUPING(inner_cte.port_id) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE inner_cte.mac_address END AS mac_address, SUM(inner_cte.ip_allocation_count) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(inner_cte.subnet_id_rows) AS subnet_id_rows FROM inner_cte GROUP BY inner_cte.tenant_id, inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.mac_address WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY tenant_id_sort, tenant_id, port_id), TenantAdminUpTotals AS ( SELECT p.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS total_admin_up_ports_with_ip FROM ports p JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL AND p.status = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.tenant_id ) SELECT dp.tenant_id, dp.port_id, dp.host, dp.vif_type, dp.ip_address, dp.window_column, dp.total_down_ports, dp.benchmark, dp.user_category, aui.mac_address, aui.ip_allocation_count, aui.subnet_id_rows, tat.total_admin_up_ports_with_ip FROM down_ports dp LEFT JOIN admin_up_ipalloc_rollup aui ON aui.port_id = dp.port_id LEFT JOIN TenantAdminUpTotals tat ON tat.tenant_id = dp.tenant_id WHERE dp.user_category = 'HIGH_USER' ORDER BY dp.total_down_ports DESC, dp.tenant_id, dp.ip_address;

question: For the top 10 security groups with the most DOWN ports, list each security group’s ID, its total number of DOWN ports, and whether any of those DOWN ports belong to a tenant that has more than one DOWN port; additionally, for the DOWN port status, include the variance of STANDARD_ATTR_ID (considering only ports with an IP allocation and a non-null STANDARD_ATTR_ID), the total number of distinct ports in that status, and whether any of those ports have floating IPs. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH PortStatusVariance AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM PORTS AS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.STATUS ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ) SELECT i.STATUS, i.standard_attr_id_variance, COUNT(DISTINCT p2.ID) AS total_ports, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT f.ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_floating_ips FROM inner_cte i JOIN PORTS p2 ON p2.STATUS = i.STATUS JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia2 ON ia2.PORT_ID = p2.ID LEFT JOIN FLOATINGIPS f ON f.FIXED_PORT_ID = p2.ID WHERE p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY i.STATUS, i.standard_attr_id_variance ORDER BY i.standard_attr_id_variance DESC LIMIT 10 ), TopSecurityGroupsDownPorts AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN') SELECT inner_cte.security_group_id, COUNT(DISTINCT inner_cte.port_id) AS total_down_ports, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT t.tenant_id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_tenant_with_multiple_down_ports FROM inner_cte LEFT JOIN (SELECT tenant_id FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT port_id) > 1) AS t ON inner_cte.tenant_id = t.tenant_id GROUP BY inner_cte.security_group_id ORDER BY total_down_ports DESC LIMIT 10 ) SELECT tsg.security_group_id, tsg.total_down_ports, tsg.has_tenant_with_multiple_down_ports, psv.STATUS AS port_status, psv.standard_attr_id_variance, psv.total_ports, psv.has_floating_ips FROM TopSecurityGroupsDownPorts tsg JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb ON sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = tsg.security_group_id JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = sgpb.PORT_ID JOIN PortStatusVariance psv ON psv.STATUS = p.STATUS WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY tsg.total_down_ports DESC, psv.standard_attr_id_variance DESC;

question: For the top 3 networks with the most subnets among RBAC entries where the action is 'access_as_shared', show each network (with its subnet count) and each subnet’s tenant ID, along with (on those same networks) the number of DOWN ports whose standard attribute ID is greater than the average standard attribute ID for DOWN ports in the same resource type, and the average of their running-sum standard attribute ID window values. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH down_ports_windowed AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), ResourceTypeAverages AS (SELECT sa.RESOURCE_TYPE, AVG(sa.ID) AS avg_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.window_column FROM inner_cte i JOIN PORTS p2 ON p2.ID = i.port_id JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa2 ON sa2.ID = p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa2.ID > (SELECT avg_standard_attr_id FROM ResourceTypeAverages rta WHERE rta.RESOURCE_TYPE = sa2.RESOURCE_TYPE) ), top_shared_network_subnets AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.OBJECT_ID AS network_id, COUNT(*) AS subnet_count FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.OBJECT_ID ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 3 ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(inner_cte.network_id) OVER (ORDER BY inner_cte.network_id) = inner_cte.network_id THEN NULL ELSE inner_cte.network_id END AS network_id, inner_cte.subnet_count, s.TENANT_ID AS subnet_tenant_id FROM inner_cte JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON s.NETWORK_ID = inner_cte.network_id ORDER BY inner_cte.network_id, s.TENANT_ID ), down_ports_on_top_shared_networks AS ( SELECT dpw.port_id, dpw.tenant_id, dpw.mac_address, dpw.window_column, tsn.network_id, tsn.subnet_count, tsn.subnet_tenant_id FROM down_ports_windowed dpw JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = dpw.port_id JOIN top_shared_network_subnets tsn ON tsn.network_id = p.NETWORK_ID ) SELECT dptsn.network_id, dptsn.subnet_count, dptsn.subnet_tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT dptsn.port_id) AS down_port_count, AVG(dptsn.window_column) AS avg_down_port_running_sum_standard_attr_ids FROM down_ports_on_top_shared_networks dptsn GROUP BY dptsn.network_id, dptsn.subnet_count, dptsn.subnet_tenant_id ORDER BY dptsn.subnet_count DESC, dptsn.network_id, dptsn.subnet_tenant_id;

question: How many of the top 10 port statuses (ranked by the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of ports’ standard attribute IDs, considering only ports that have both a security group port binding and a port security binding) are DOWN, how many of those DOWN statuses have any floating IPs allocated, and how many rows in the DOWN-and-security-group breakdown (by device owner, including subtotals) correspond to port status DOWN? Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS
