SQL: WITH down_ports_top10 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN') SELECT inner_cte.security_group_id, COUNT(DISTINCT inner_cte.port_id) AS total_down_ports, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT t.tenant_id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_tenant_with_multiple_down_ports FROM inner_cte LEFT JOIN (SELECT tenant_id FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT port_id) > 1) AS t ON inner_cte.tenant_id = t.tenant_id GROUP BY inner_cte.security_group_id ORDER BY total_down_ports DESC LIMIT 10 ), sg_geomean AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, EXP(AVG(LN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID))) AS geometric_mean_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID > 0 GROUP BY s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY geometric_mean_standard_attr_id DESC ) SELECT inner_cte.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, inner_cte.geometric_mean_standard_attr_id, avg_sg.avg_geometric_mean_standard_attr_id FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(geometric_mean_standard_attr_id) AS avg_geometric_mean_standard_attr_id FROM inner_cte ) AS avg_sg ON 1 = 1 ORDER BY inner_cte.geometric_mean_standard_attr_id DESC ) SELECT dpt.security_group_id, dpt.total_down_ports, dpt.has_tenant_with_multiple_down_ports, sg.geometric_mean_standard_attr_id, sg.avg_geometric_mean_standard_attr_id FROM down_ports_top10 AS dpt LEFT JOIN sg_geomean AS sg ON dpt.security_group_id = sg.security_group_id ORDER BY dpt.total_down_ports DESC;

question: For tenants that have ports on host "drive-59", list the DOWN ports that belong to security groups whose DOWN-port count is above the average across security groups, showing the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, security group ID, the port’s rank within its security group (ordered by port ID), the security group’s DOWN-port total, the tenant’s total distinct ports on "drive-59", and whether the tenant has any ports with port security enabled. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH down_ports_sg AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN'), sg_counts AS ( SELECT security_group_id, COUNT(*) AS down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY security_group_id ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.security_group_id, i.window_column, c.down_ports FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN sg_counts AS c ON i.security_group_id = c.security_group_id WHERE c.down_ports > (SELECT AVG(down_ports) FROM sg_counts)), host_drive59_tenants AS (WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' ) SELECT i.TENANT_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT i.PORT_ID) AS total_ports, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT psb.PORT_ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_port_security_enabled FROM inner_cte AS i LEFT JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON i.PORT_ID = psb.PORT_ID GROUP BY i.TENANT_ID ORDER BY total_ports DESC) SELECT d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.mac_address, d.security_group_id, d.window_column AS port_rank_within_security_group_by_port_id, d.down_ports AS down_ports_in_security_group, h.total_ports AS total_ports_on_drive_59_for_tenant, h.has_port_security_enabled FROM down_ports_sg AS d JOIN host_drive59_tenants AS h ON d.tenant_id = h.tenant_id;

question: For each tenant that (1) has at least one port bound to a security group with admin_state_up = 1 and (2) has at least one port that is DOWN with port security enabled, list the tenant ID, the total number of DOWN ports with port security enabled and the average of that count across tenants, the total number of admin-up ports with security-group bindings along with total security-group bindings and DNS records and the average of that port count across tenants, and the ratio (rounded to 2 decimals) of DOWN+secure ports to admin-up security-group-bound ports.
SQL: WITH down_secure_ports AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 ) SELECT p.tenant_id AS ports_tenant_id, COUNT(p.id) AS total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled, avg_counts.avg_down_secure_port_count FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id JOIN ( SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_down_secure_port_count FROM ( SELECT p2.tenant_id, COUNT(p2.id) AS port_count FROM ports p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings psb2 ON p2.id = psb2.port_id WHERE p2.status = 'DOWN' AND psb2.port_security_enabled = 1 GROUP BY p2.tenant_id ) AS sub ) AS avg_counts ON 1 = 1 CROSS JOIN inner_cte WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND psb.port_security_enabled = 1 GROUP BY p.tenant_id, avg_counts.avg_down_secure_port_count ), sg_admin_up_ports AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name) SELECT inner_cte.tenant_id, COUNT(inner_cte.port_id) AS total_ports_with_sg_binding_admin_up, SUM(inner_cte.security_group_binding_count) AS total_security_group_bindings, SUM(inner_cte.dns_record_count) AS total_dns_records, avg_ports.avg_port_count AS avg_ports_with_sg_binding_admin_up_per_tenant FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count FROM ( SELECT COUNT(port_id) AS port_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS sub ) AS avg_ports GROUP BY inner_cte.tenant_id, avg_ports.avg_port_count ) SELECT sap.tenant_id, dsp.total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled, dsp.avg_down_secure_port_count, sap.total_ports_with_sg_binding_admin_up, sap.total_security_group_bindings, sap.total_dns_records, sap.avg_ports_with_sg_binding_admin_up_per_tenant, ROUND( dsp.total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled / NULLIF(sap.total_ports_with_sg_binding_admin_up, 0), 2 ) AS down_secure_to_sg_admin_up_port_ratio FROM sg_admin_up_ports sap JOIN down_secure_ports dsp ON sap.tenant_id = dsp.ports_tenant_id ORDER BY down_secure_to_sg_admin_up_port_ratio DESC;

question: Show (1) the network-status rollup (by network status and whether the network is External vs Internal) with the variance and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED for networks that have security bindings, and (2) the IPv4 subnet rollup (by subnet name and whether the subnet’s standard attribute has an updated-at timestamp) with the row counts—return both result sets together in one output. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH NetworkStatusStats AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.STATUS AS network_status, VARIANCE(nsb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) AS port_security_enabled_variance, STDDEV(nsb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) AS port_security_enabled_stddev FROM NETWORKS AS n JOIN NETWORKSECURITYBINDINGS AS nsb ON n.ID = nsb.NETWORK_ID GROUP BY n.STATUS ORDER BY port_security_enabled_variance DESC ), NetworkStatusExternal AS ( SELECT n.status, CASE WHEN en.network_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'External' ELSE 'Internal' END AS external_status, VARIANCE(nsb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) AS port_security_enabled_variance, STDDEV(nsb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) AS port_security_enabled_stddev FROM networks n JOIN networksecuritybindings nsb ON n.id = nsb.network_id LEFT JOIN externalnetworks en ON n.id = en.network_id GROUP BY n.status, external_status ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(nse.status) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE nse.status END AS network_status, CASE WHEN GROUPING(nse.external_status) = 1 AND GROUPING(nse.status) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE nse.external_status END AS external_status, VARIANCE(nse.port_security_enabled_variance) AS port_security_enabled_variance, STDDEV(nse.port_security_enabled_stddev) AS port_security_enabled_stddev FROM NetworkStatusExternal nse CROSS JOIN inner_cte GROUP BY nse.status, nse.external_status WITH ROLLUP ), SubnetUpdateStats AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT s.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY sa.UPDATED_AT ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES AS sa ON sa.ID = s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4), SubnetUpdateBuckets AS ( SELECT i.NAME, CASE WHEN sa.UPDATED_AT IS NOT NULL THEN 'Has Updated Timestamp' ELSE 'No Updated Timestamp' END AS updated_bucket, COUNT(*) AS total_rows FROM inner_cte i JOIN SUBNETS s ON s.NAME = i.NAME JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID GROUP BY i.NAME, updated_bucket ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(NAME) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE NAME END AS NAME, CASE WHEN GROUPING(updated_bucket) = 1 AND GROUPING(NAME) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE updated_bucket END AS updated_bucket, SUM(total_rows) AS total_rows FROM SubnetUpdateBuckets GROUP BY NAME, updated_bucket WITH ROLLUP ) SELECT nss.network_status, nss.external_status, nss.port_security_enabled_variance, nss.port_security_enabled_stddev, sus.NAME AS subnet_name, sus.updated_bucket, sus.total_rows FROM NetworkStatusStats nss CROSS JOIN SubnetUpdateStats sus;

question: For the top 10 tenants with the highest number of networks marked as default external networks (IS_DEFAULT = 0), show each tenant’s ID, the total count of those default external networks, the minimum MTU among those networks, and (considering only ACTIVE networks) the latest standard attribute UPDATED_AT timestamp for that tenant. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH active_network_latest_stdattr AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT tenant_id, MAX(standard_attr_updated_at) AS latest_standard_attr_updated_at FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ), top10_default_external_tenants AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT e.NETWORK_ID, e.IS_DEFAULT, n.TENANT_ID, n.NAME, n.STATUS, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP, n.MTU, n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID, MIN(n.MTU) OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.TENANT_ID) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0 ) SELECT i.TENANT_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT i.NETWORK_ID) AS total_default_external_networks, MIN(i.MTU) AS min_mtu_in_tenant FROM inner_cte i GROUP BY i.TENANT_ID ORDER BY total_default_external_networks DESC LIMIT 10 ) SELECT t.TENANT_ID, t.total_default_external_networks, t.min_mtu_in_tenant, a.latest_standard_attr_updated_at FROM top10_default_external_tenants t JOIN active_network_latest_stdattr a ON t.TENANT_ID = a.tenant_id ORDER BY t.total_default_external_networks DESC;

question: For ports bound to security group ID 0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c, list each port’s ID, status, allocated IP address, and the running sum of its standard attribute ID within its network (ordered by standard attribute ID); also include the owning tenant ID, that tenant’s total number of such ports and the average of these per-tenant totals across all tenants, and for the same port status report the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of standard attribute IDs (for ports that have both a security group port binding and a port security binding) along with the average coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) across all statuses. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH subq1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.STATUS AS port_status, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' ) SELECT inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.port_status, inner_cte.ip_address, inner_cte.window_column, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, COUNT(p.ID) AS total_ports_for_tenant_in_sg, avg_ports.avg_port_count AS avg_ports_per_tenant_in_sg FROM inner_cte JOIN PORTS p ON inner_cte.port_id = p.ID JOIN ( SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count FROM ( SELECT COUNT(p2.ID) AS port_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb2 JOIN PORTS p2 ON sgpb2.PORT_ID = p2.ID WHERE sgpb2.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' GROUP BY p2.TENANT_ID ) AS sub ) AS avg_ports ON 1 = 1 GROUP BY inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.port_status, inner_cte.ip_address, inner_cte.window_column, p.TENANT_ID, avg_ports.avg_port_count ), subq2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC) SELECT inner_cte.status, inner_cte.coefficient_of_variation, avg_cov.avg_coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(coefficient_of_variation) AS avg_coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte ) AS avg_cov ON 1 = 1 ORDER BY inner_cte.coefficient_of_variation DESC ) SELECT subq1.port_id, subq1.port_status, subq1.ip_address, subq1.window_column, subq1.tenant_id, subq1.total_ports_for_tenant_in_sg, subq1.avg_ports_per_tenant_in_sg, subq2.coefficient_of_variation, subq2.avg_coefficient_of_variation FROM subq1 JOIN subq2 ON subq1.port_status = subq2.status;

question: For the allowed address pairs on port ID `25d421c1-c76d-4c26-9550-9f871a1d5034`, list each allowed address pair’s MAC address and IP address, the port ID, and the bound security group ID, along with (a) the running average of that port’s standard attribute ID (ordered by allowed address pair IP) and its deviation from the overall average running average, and (b) the geometric mean of standard attribute IDs for ports bound to that same security group (considering only standard attribute IDs > 0) and its deviation from the overall average geometric mean across security groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH sg_geom AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, EXP(AVG(LN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID))) AS geometric_mean_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID > 0 GROUP BY s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY geometric_mean_standard_attr_id DESC), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(geometric_mean_standard_attr_id) AS avg_geometric_mean_standard_attr_id FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, i.geometric_mean_standard_attr_id, (i.geometric_mean_standard_attr_id - a.avg_geometric_mean_standard_attr_id) AS deviation_from_avg_geometric_mean FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a ORDER BY deviation_from_avg_geometric_mean DESC ), port_aap_window AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT aap.MAC_ADDRESS AS allowed_mac_address, aap.IP_ADDRESS AS allowed_ip_address, p.ID AS port_id, sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS security_group_id, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY aap.IP_ADDRESS ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN ALLOWEDADDRESSPAIRS AS aap ON p.ID = aap.PORT_ID WHERE p.ID = '25d421c1-c76d-4c26-9550-9f871a1d5034' ORDER BY aap.IP_ADDRESS ), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(window_column) AS avg_window_column FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.allowed_mac_address, i.allowed_ip_address, i.port_id, i.security_group_id, i.window_column, (i.window_column - a.avg_window_column) AS deviation_from_avg_window FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a ORDER BY i.allowed_ip_address ) SELECT p.allowed_mac_address, p.allowed_ip_address, p.port_id, p.security_group_id, p.window_column, p.deviation_from_avg_window, g.geometric_mean_standard_attr_id, g.deviation_from_avg_geometric_mean FROM port_aap_window p JOIN sg_geom g ON p.security_group_id = g.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.allowed_ip_address;

question: For ACTIVE networks, list the network name, status, and admin_state_up together with each RBAC action and target tenant, the number of distinct RBAC target tenants per network, and the dense-rank value; restrict the results to networks whose owning tenant is among the top 10 tenants by total IPv4 subnet count (considering only IPv4 subnets with a non-null standard-attribute updated-at), and also show that tenant’s total IPv4 subnet count and whether they have any such updated standard-attribute record. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH tenant_ipv4 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY sa.UPDATED_AT ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES AS sa ON sa.ID = s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ) SELECT s.TENANT_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT s.ID) AS total_ipv4_subnets, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT sa.ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_any_updated_standard_attribute FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES AS sa ON sa.ID = s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID JOIN inner_cte AS ic ON ic.NAME = s.NAME WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 AND sa.UPDATED_AT IS NOT NULL GROUP BY s.TENANT_ID ORDER BY total_ipv4_subnets DESC LIMIT 10 ), active_network_rbac AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.name, n.status, n.admin_state_up, r.action, r.target_tenant, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY n.id ORDER BY n.id) AS window_column FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE'), rbac_counts AS ( SELECT n.id AS network_id, COUNT(DISTINCT r.target_tenant) AS distinct_target_tenants FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n.id ) SELECT i.name, i.status, i.admin_state_up, i.action, i.target_tenant, c.distinct_target_tenants, i.window_column FROM inner_cte i JOIN rbac_counts c ON c.network_id = (SELECT n2.id FROM networks n2 WHERE n2.name = i.name AND n2.status = i.status AND n2.admin_state_up = i.admin_state_up LIMIT 1) ), network_tenant_map AS ( SELECT DISTINCT n.id AS network_id, n.tenant_id FROM networks n WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT anr.name AS network_name, anr.status AS network_status, anr.admin_state_up, anr.action AS rbac_action, anr.target_tenant, anr.distinct_target_tenants, anr.window_column AS network_dense_rank, t.total_ipv4_subnets, t.has_any_updated_standard_attribute FROM active_network_rbac anr JOIN networks n ON n.name = anr.name AND n.status = anr.status AND n.admin_state_up = anr.admin_state_up JOIN network_tenant_map ntm ON ntm.network_id = n.id JOIN tenant_ipv4 t ON t.tenant_id = ntm.tenant_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE';

question: For each ACTIVE network that has an RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', list the network name, status, admin_state_up, RBAC target tenant, dense-rank within the network ID, the network MTU and its deviation from the average MTU across all ACTIVE networks, and also include (by matching on status) the status-level average and variance of MTU computed from external networks shared via 'access_as_shared'. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.status, AVG(n.mtu) AS avg_mtu, VARIANCE(n.mtu) AS mtu_variance FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.network_id = n.id JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE r.action = 'access_as_shared' AND n.mtu IS NOT NULL GROUP BY n.status ORDER BY mtu_variance DESC) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(status) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE status END AS status, AVG(avg_mtu) AS avg_mtu, AVG(mtu_variance) AS mtu_variance FROM inner_cte GROUP BY status WITH ROLLUP ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.name, n.status, n.admin_state_up, r.action, r.target_tenant, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY n.id ORDER BY n.id) AS window_column FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE'), ActiveNetworkMTU AS ( SELECT n.id AS network_id, n.mtu FROM networks n WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' ), AverageActiveMTU AS ( SELECT AVG(mtu) AS avg_mtu FROM ActiveNetworkMTU ) SELECT i.name, i.status, i.admin_state_up, i.action, i.target_tenant, i.window_column, anm.mtu, (anm.mtu - aam.avg_mtu) AS deviation_from_avg_mtu FROM inner_cte i JOIN networks n ON n.name = i.name AND n.status = i.status AND n.admin_state_up = i.admin_state_up JOIN ActiveNetworkMTU anm ON anm.network_id = n.id CROSS JOIN AverageActiveMTU aam ) SELECT q2.name, q2.status, q2.admin_state_up, q2.action, q2.target_tenant, q2.window_column, q2.mtu, q2.deviation_from_avg_mtu, q1.avg_mtu AS status_level_avg_mtu_for_external_shared, q1.mtu_variance AS status_level_mtu_variance_for_external_shared FROM q2 JOIN q1 ON q1.status = q2.status WHERE q2.action = 'access_as_shared' ORDER BY q2.deviation_from_avg_mtu DESC;

question: For each subnet (by subnet name) that belongs to a network with an RBAC action of 'access_as_shared' and has a maximum IP version greater than 3 (grouped by subnet name and gateway IP), show the subnet name, gateway IP, the group’s maximum IP version, the total number of such subnet-name/gateway-IP groups, the deviation of that maximum IP version from the overall average maximum IP version, and also the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of DNS nameserver order values for that subnet (IPv4 only) along with its deviation from the average coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) across all IPv4 subnets. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, STDDEV(d.ORDER) / NULLIF(AVG(d.ORDER), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s.id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name HAVING AVG(d.ORDER) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(coefficient_of_variation) AS avg_coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.subnet_name, i.coefficient_of_variation, (i.coefficient_of_variation - a.avg_coefficient_of_variation) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a ORDER BY deviation_from_avg DESC ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT s.name, MAX(s.ip_version) AS max_ip_version, s.gateway_ip FROM NETWORKRBACS n JOIN SUBNETS s ON n.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.action = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY s.name, s.gateway_ip HAVING MAX(s.ip_version) > 3), avg_cte AS (SELECT AVG(max_ip_version) AS avg_max_ip_version, COUNT(*) AS total_groups FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.name, i.gateway_ip, i.max_ip_version, a.total_groups, (i.max_ip_version - a.avg_max_ip_version) AS deviation_from_avg_max_ip_version FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a ) SELECT q2.name AS subnet_name, q2.gateway_ip, q2.max_ip_version, q2.total_groups, q2.deviation_from_avg_max_ip_version, q1.coefficient_of_variation, q1.deviation_from_avg FROM q2 JOIN q1 ON q1.subnet_name = q2.name ORDER BY q2.deviation_from_avg_max_ip_version DESC, q1.deviation_from_avg DESC;

question: For DOWN ports that have a running sum of standard attribute IDs (within each standard-attribute resource type ordered by standard attribute ID) greater than the average running sum across all DOWN ports, list the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the running-sum value, and—restricted to tenants in the top 10 by maximum binding-count range across their port statuses (considering only ports with at least one port security binding)—each tenant’s maximum binding-count range and whether they have any floating IPs allocated to their ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH down_ports_window AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT port_id, tenant_id, mac_address, window_column FROM inner_cte WHERE window_column > (SELECT AVG(window_column) FROM inner_cte) ), top_tenants_binding_fips AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.status, MAX(ps.binding_count) - MIN(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_range, VARIANCE(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_variance, STDDEV(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_stddev FROM ports AS p JOIN ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id GROUP BY p2.id ) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id GROUP BY p.status ORDER BY binding_count_range DESC ) SELECT p.tenant_id, MAX(inner_cte.binding_count_range) AS max_binding_count_range_across_statuses, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT f.id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_floating_ips FROM ports AS p JOIN ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id GROUP BY p2.id ) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id JOIN inner_cte ON p.status = inner_cte.status LEFT JOIN floatingips AS f ON p.id = f.fixed_port_id GROUP BY p.tenant_id ORDER BY max_binding_count_range_across_statuses DESC LIMIT 10 ) SELECT dpw.port_id, dpw.tenant_id, dpw.mac_address, dpw.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_ids, ttb.max_binding_count_range_across_statuses, ttb.has_floating_ips FROM down_ports_window dpw JOIN top_tenants_binding_fips ttb ON dpw.tenant_id = ttb.tenant_id ORDER BY ttb.max_binding_count_range_across_statuses DESC, dpw.window_column DESC;

question: For VIF types whose number of administratively up ports is greater than the average administratively up port count across all VIF types, list each administratively up port’s port ID, host, VIF type, VNIC type, tenant ID, network ID, MAC address, status, device owner, and the 2-preceding/2-following windowed average of standard attribute ID (partitioned by VIF type and ordered by standard attribute ID), along with (for the same VIF type) the highest 2-preceding/2-following windowed average of the admin_state_up flag (ordered by MAC address) among ports that are DOWN. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, b.VNIC_TYPE, p.TENANT_ID, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 ), VifCounts AS ( SELECT VIF_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS vif_port_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY VIF_TYPE ), OverallAvg AS ( SELECT AVG(vif_port_count) AS avg_vif_port_count FROM VifCounts ) SELECT i.PORT_ID, i.HOST, i.VIF_TYPE, i.VNIC_TYPE, i.TENANT_ID, i.NETWORK_ID, i.MAC_ADDRESS, i.STATUS, i.DEVICE_OWNER, i.window_column FROM inner_cte i JOIN VifCounts vc ON i.VIF_TYPE = vc.VIF_TYPE CROSS JOIN OverallAvg oa WHERE vc.vif_port_count > oa.avg_vif_port_count ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS) SELECT VIF_TYPE, MAX(window_column) AS max_windowed_avg_admin_state_up FROM inner_cte GROUP BY VIF_TYPE ) SELECT q1.PORT_ID, q1.HOST, q1.VIF_TYPE, q1.VNIC_TYPE, q1.TENANT_ID, q1.NETWORK_ID, q1.MAC_ADDRESS, q1.STATUS, q1.DEVICE_OWNER, q1.window_column AS avg_standard_attr_id_window_2p2f, q2.max_windowed_avg_admin_state_up FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q1.VIF_TYPE = q2.VIF_TYPE;

question: List IPv4 subnets (by subnet name) that are included either because they are in the top 10 by route-count range or because their DNS nameserver order variance is above the overall IPv4 average, showing the tenant ID and whether DHCP is enabled, along with the route-count range/variance/stddev or the DNS order average/variance and a reason label for inclusion. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH TopRouteRangeSubnets AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(route_count) - MIN(route_count) AS route_count_range, VARIANCE(route_count) AS route_count_variance, STDDEV(route_count) AS route_count_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN ( SELECT sr.SUBNET_ID, COUNT(*) AS route_count FROM SUBNETROUTES AS sr GROUP BY sr.SUBNET_ID, sr.NEXTHOP ) AS route_stats ON s.ID = route_stats.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY route_count_range DESC ) SELECT inner_cte.subnet_name, inner_cte.route_count_range, inner_cte.route_count_variance, inner_cte.route_count_stddev, s.tenant_id, CASE WHEN s.enable_dhcp = 1 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS dhcp_enabled FROM inner_cte JOIN subnets s ON s.name = inner_cte.subnet_name WHERE s.ip_version = 4 ORDER BY inner_cte.route_count_range DESC LIMIT 10 ), HighDnsVarianceSubnets AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, AVG(d.ORDER) AS avg_dns_order, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS dns_order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.ID = d.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY dns_order_variance DESC) SELECT subnet_name, avg_dns_order, dns_order_variance FROM inner_cte WHERE dns_order_variance > (SELECT AVG(dns_order_variance) FROM inner_cte) ORDER BY dns_order_variance DESC ), CombinedSubnets AS ( SELECT trrs.subnet_name, trrs.tenant_id, trrs.dhcp_enabled, trrs.route_count_range, trrs.route_count_variance, trrs.route_count_stddev, NULL AS avg_dns_order, NULL AS dns_order_variance, 'Top Route-Count Range' AS reason FROM TopRouteRangeSubnets trrs UNION ALL SELECT hdvs.subnet_name, s.tenant_id, CASE WHEN s.enable_dhcp = 1 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS dhcp_enabled, NULL AS route_count_range, NULL AS route_count_variance, NULL AS route_count_stddev, hdvs.avg_dns_order, hdvs.dns_order_variance, 'High DNS Order Variance' AS reason FROM HighDnsVarianceSubnets hdvs JOIN subnets s ON s.name = hdvs.subnet_name AND s.ip_version = 4 ) SELECT * FROM CombinedSubnets ORDER BY subnet_name, reason;

question: For tenants classified as HIGH_USER based on their number of DOWN ports (at least 50% above the average across tenants), list each DOWN port’s port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and its row number ordered by IP address (with a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row). Also include the tenant’s total DOWN ports, the average DOWN-port benchmark, and the tenant’s administrative-status rollup totals (total qualifying ports, total IP allocations, and total subnet-id rows). Do not return any rounded answers. Classify the tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'.
SQL: WITH down_ports_detail AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), TenantDownPorts AS ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT port_id) AS total_down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ), AverageDownPorts AS ( SELECT AVG(total_down_ports) AS avg_down_ports FROM TenantDownPorts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.window_column, tdp.total_down_ports, adp.avg_down_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tdp.total_down_ports > adp.avg_down_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tdp.total_down_ports < adp.avg_down_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM inner_cte i JOIN TenantDownPorts tdp ON i.tenant_id = tdp.tenant_id CROSS JOIN AverageDownPorts adp ), tenant_admin_rollup AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ia.subnet_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS subnet_id_rows FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ), TenantPortRollup AS ( SELECT ic.tenant_id, CASE WHEN p.admin_state_up = 1 THEN 'Up' ELSE 'Down' END AS admin_status, COUNT(DISTINCT ic.port_id) AS total_ports, SUM(ic.ip_allocation_count) AS total_ip_allocations, SUM(ic.subnet_id_rows) AS total_subnet_id_rows FROM inner_cte ic JOIN ports p ON p.id = ic.port_id GROUP BY ic.tenant_id, admin_status ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(tenant_id) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE tenant_id END AS tenant_id, CASE WHEN GROUPING(admin_status) = 1 AND GROUPING(tenant_id) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' WHEN GROUPING(admin_status) = 1 AND GROUPING(tenant_id) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE admin_status END AS admin_status, SUM(total_ports) AS total_ports, SUM(total_ip_allocations) AS total_ip_allocations, SUM(total_subnet_id_rows) AS total_subnet_id_rows FROM TenantPortRollup GROUP BY tenant_id, admin_status WITH ROLLUP ) SELECT dpd.port_id, dpd.tenant_id, dpd.host, dpd.vif_type, dpd.ip_address, dpd.window_column, dpd.total_down_ports, dpd.benchmark, dpd.user_category, tar.admin_status, tar.total_ports, tar.total_ip_allocations, tar.total_subnet_id_rows FROM down_ports_detail dpd LEFT JOIN tenant_admin_rollup tar ON tar.tenant_id = dpd.tenant_id WHERE dpd.user_category = 'HIGH_USER';

question: For ports whose status is 'DOWN' and that belong to security groups where the number of DOWN ports is greater than the average DOWN-port count per security group, list each port’s ID, name, tenant ID, MAC address, allocated IP address, subnet ID, the average port ID within its port-ID group ordered by IP address, the total allocated IPs in that subnet and its deviation from the average subnet allocation count, plus the security group ID, the port’s rank within that security group by port ID, and the security group’s DOWN-port count. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ia.SUBNET_ID AS subnet_id, AVG(p.ID) OVER (PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ), SubnetAllocations AS ( SELECT ia.subnet_id, COUNT(DISTINCT ia.ip_address) AS allocated_ips FROM IPALLOCATIONS ia GROUP BY ia.subnet_id ), AverageAllocations AS ( SELECT AVG(allocated_ips) AS avg_ips FROM SubnetAllocations ) SELECT i.port_id, i.port_name, i.mac_address, i.ip_address, i.subnet_id, i.window_column, sa.allocated_ips AS subnet_allocated_ips, (sa.allocated_ips - aa.avg_ips) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i JOIN SubnetAllocations sa ON i.subnet_id = sa.subnet_id CROSS JOIN AverageAllocations aa ORDER BY i.ip_address ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN'), sg_counts AS ( SELECT security_group_id, COUNT(*) AS down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY security_group_id ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.security_group_id, i.window_column, c.down_ports FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN sg_counts AS c ON i.security_group_id = c.security_group_id WHERE c.down_ports > (SELECT AVG(down_ports) FROM sg_counts) ) SELECT q1.port_id, q1.port_name, q2.tenant_id, q1.mac_address, q1.ip_address, q1.subnet_id, q1.window_column AS avg_port_id_within_port_id_group_ordered_by_ip, q1.subnet_allocated_ips, q1.deviation_from_avg, q2.security_group_id, q2.window_column AS rank_within_security_group_by_port_id, q2.down_ports FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q1.port_id = q2.port_id ORDER BY q1.ip_address, q2.security_group_id, q1.port_id;

question: Considering only ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports', for each (port status, device owner) group whose port count is greater than the overall average port count across all such groups, return the port status, device owner, number of ports, earliest standard attribute updated timestamp, and the deviation of that group’s port count from the overall average. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH deviation_by_status_owner AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER), avg_cte AS (SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.earliest_standard_attr_update, (i.port_count - a.avg_port_count) AS deviation_from_avg_port_count FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a ), above_avg_groups AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER), GroupAverage AS ( SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.earliest_standard_attr_update FROM inner_cte i WHERE i.port_count > (SELECT avg_port_count FROM GroupAverage) ) SELECT a.port_status, a.device_owner, a.port_count, a.earliest_standard_attr_update, d.deviation_from_avg_port_count FROM above_avg_groups a JOIN deviation_by_status_owner d ON d.port_status = a.port_status AND d.device_owner = a.device_owner AND d.port_count = a.port_count AND d.earliest_standard_attr_update = a.earliest_standard_attr_update;

question: For ACTIVE networks, show the network ID, network name, tenant ID, admin_state_up flag, MTU, the standard attribute updated_at timestamp, the row number within each tenant ordered by network name, the overall average MTU across all ACTIVE networks (as a benchmark), and an MTU category (ABOVE_AVG_MTU/BELOW_AVG_MTU/AT_AVG_MTU); additionally, only include networks that have DOWN ports whose 2-preceding/2-following window average of port admin_state_up (partitioned by VIF type and ordered by MAC address) is greater than the overall average of that window average for the same VIF type, and list those ports’ name, MAC address, admin_state_up, binding host, VIF type, and window average. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE'), AvgMtu AS (SELECT AVG(mtu) AS avg_mtu FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.network_id, i.network_name, i.tenant_id, i.admin_state_up, i.mtu, i.standard_attr_updated_at, i.window_column, a.avg_mtu AS benchmark_avg_mtu, CASE WHEN i.mtu > a.avg_mtu THEN 'ABOVE_AVG_MTU' WHEN i.mtu < a.avg_mtu THEN 'BELOW_AVG_MTU' ELSE 'AT_AVG_MTU' END AS mtu_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN AvgMtu a ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS), VifTypeAverages AS ( SELECT VIF_TYPE, AVG(window_column) AS avg_window_column FROM inner_cte GROUP BY VIF_TYPE ) SELECT i.NAME, i.MAC_ADDRESS, i.ADMIN_STATE_UP, i.HOST, i.VIF_TYPE, i.window_column FROM inner_cte i JOIN VifTypeAverages v ON i.VIF_TYPE = v.VIF_TYPE WHERE i.window_column > v.avg_window_column ORDER BY i.MAC_ADDRESS ), q2_ports AS ( SELECT p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, q2.NAME AS port_name, q2.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, q2.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS port_admin_state_up, q2.HOST AS binding_host, q2.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, q2.window_column AS port_admin_state_up_window_avg FROM q2 JOIN PORTS p ON p.MAC_ADDRESS = q2.MAC_ADDRESS AND p.NAME = q2.NAME WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT q1.network_id, q1.network_name, q1.tenant_id, q1.admin_state_up AS network_admin_state_up, q1.mtu, q1.standard_attr_updated_at, q1.window_column AS tenant_network_name_rownum, q1.benchmark_avg_mtu, q1.mtu_category, q2_ports.port_name, q2_ports.mac_address, q2_ports.port_admin_state_up, q2_ports.binding_host, q2_ports.vif_type, q2_ports.port_admin_state_up_window_avg FROM q1 JOIN q2_ports ON q1.network_id = q2_ports.network_id ORDER BY q1.tenant_id, q1.network_name, q2_ports.mac_address;

question: For the “haproxy” provider, which ONLINE load balancers have total connections above the average ONLINE total connections for their provider and also have bytes in above the average bytes in across all “haproxy” load balancers; return the load balancer ID, name, provider name, VIP address, the provider rank (by total connections), bytes in, total connections, and the haproxy row-number window ordered by load balancer name (2 preceding to 1 following). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT lb.ID AS loadbalancer_id, lb.NAME AS loadbalancer_name, pra.PROVIDER_NAME AS provider_name, lb.VIP_ADDRESS AS vip_address, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY pra.PROVIDER_NAME ORDER BY stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS ) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb ON stats.LOADBALANCER_ID = lb.ID JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE lb.OPERATING_STATUS = 'ONLINE' ), ProviderAverages AS ( SELECT pra.PROVIDER_NAME AS provider_name, AVG(stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS) AS avg_total_connections FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb ON stats.LOADBALANCER_ID = lb.ID JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE lb.OPERATING_STATUS = 'ONLINE' GROUP BY pra.PROVIDER_NAME ) SELECT i.loadbalancer_id, i.loadbalancer_name, i.provider_name, i.vip_address, i.window_column FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats ON stats.LOADBALANCER_ID = i.loadbalancer_id WHERE stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS > ( SELECT pa.avg_total_connections FROM ProviderAverages AS pa WHERE pa.provider_name = i.provider_name ) ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT lb.NAME AS loadbalancer_name, lb.VIP_ADDRESS AS vip_address, stats.BYTES_IN AS bytes_in, stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS AS total_connections, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY lb.NAME ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb ON stats.LOADBALANCER_ID = lb.ID JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' ), haproxy_avg AS ( SELECT AVG(stats2.BYTES_IN * 1.0) AS avg_bytes_in FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats2 JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb2 ON stats2.LOADBALANCER_ID = lb2.ID JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra2 ON lb2.ID = pra2.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra2.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' ) SELECT i.loadbalancer_name, i.vip_address, i.bytes_in, i.total_connections, i.window_column FROM inner_cte AS i CROSS JOIN haproxy_avg AS a WHERE i.bytes_in > a.avg_bytes_in ORDER BY i.loadbalancer_name ) SELECT q1.loadbalancer_id, q1.loadbalancer_name, q1.provider_name, q1.vip_address, q1.window_column AS provider_rank_by_total_connections, q2.bytes_in, q2.total_connections, q2.window_column AS haproxy_row_number_window FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q1.loadbalancer_name = q2.loadbalancer_name AND q1.vip_address = q2.vip_address WHERE q1.provider_name = 'haproxy';

question: For networks marked as default external networks (IS_DEFAULT = 0), return the network name and dense rank (ordered by RBAC action using a window frame of the current row and the 2 preceding rows) only for those networks whose dense rank is greater than the average dense rank across all such networks, and also include the total number of such networks and the average number of such networks per RBAC action. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH RankAboveAvg AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY r.ACTION ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.ID = r.OBJECT_ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0) SELECT NAME, window_column FROM inner_cte WHERE window_column > (SELECT AVG(window_column) FROM inner_cte)), AllDefaultExternalNetworkRanks AS (WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY r.ACTION ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.ID = r.OBJECT_ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0 ) SELECT inner_cte.NAME, inner_cte.window_column, COUNT(*) AS total_networks, avg_counts.avg_networks_per_action FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(action_count) AS avg_networks_per_action FROM ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS action_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY window_column ) AS sub ) AS avg_counts ON 1 = 1 GROUP BY inner_cte.NAME, inner_cte.window_column, avg_counts.avg_networks_per_action) SELECT a.NAME, a.window_column, a.total_networks, a.avg_networks_per_action FROM AllDefaultExternalNetworkRanks a JOIN RankAboveAvg r ON r.NAME = a.NAME AND r.window_column = a.window_column;

question: For ports that (1) are bound to a security group and have admin_state_up = 1 and (2) are also in DOWN status, list the port ID, tenant ID, port name, the port’s security group binding count, the total DNS record count for the port, the deviation of that binding count from the average across all admin_state_up = 1 security-group-bound ports, and also include the port MAC address, the running sum of standard attribute ID within each security group, the tenant’s total number of DOWN ports, the average DOWN-port count across tenants as a benchmark, and the tenant category (HIGH_USER/LOW_USER/AVERAGE_USER). Do not return any rounded answers. Categorize each tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'.
SQL: WITH sg_admin_ports AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(security_group_binding_count) AS avg_sg_binding_count FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.port_name, i.security_group_binding_count, i.dns_record_count, (i.security_group_binding_count - a.avg_sg_binding_count) AS deviation_from_avg_sg_binding_count FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a), down_ports_by_sg AS (WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), TenantDownPorts AS ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT port_id) AS total_down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ), AverageDownPorts AS ( SELECT AVG(total_down_ports) AS avg_down_ports FROM TenantDownPorts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.window_column, tdp.total_down_ports, adp.avg_down_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tdp.total_down_ports > adp.avg_down_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tdp.total_down_ports < adp.avg_down_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM inner_cte i JOIN TenantDownPorts tdp ON i.tenant_id = tdp.tenant_id CROSS JOIN AverageDownPorts adp) SELECT sap.port_id, sap.tenant_id, sap.port_name, sap.security_group_binding_count, sap.dns_record_count, sap.deviation_from_avg_sg_binding_count, dps.mac_address, dps.window_column, dps.total_down_ports, dps.benchmark, dps.user_category FROM sg_admin_ports sap JOIN down_ports_by_sg dps ON sap.port_id = dps.port_id AND sap.tenant_id = dps.tenant_id;

question: For ports on host "drive-59", list each port’s port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, running sum of standard attribute IDs within its VIF type (ordered by standard attribute ID), the total number of ports in that VIF type, and the deviation from the VIF-type average running sum; also show, for the same tenant, the tenant’s count of ports that are DOWN with port security enabled, the overall average of that count across tenants (benchmark), the tenant’s HIGH/LOW/AVERAGE user category, and the overall total number of DOWN ports with port security enabled. Do not return any rounded answers. Classify each tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'.
SQL: WITH port_vif_running_sums AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' ), VifTypeStats AS ( SELECT b.VIF_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS ports_in_vif_type, AVG(ic.window_column) AS avg_running_sum_in_vif_type FROM inner_cte ic JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON b.PORT_ID = ic.PORT_ID GROUP BY b.VIF_TYPE ) SELECT ic.PORT_ID, ic.TENANT_ID, ic.MAC_ADDRESS, ic.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id, vts.ports_in_vif_type, (ic.window_column - vts.avg_running_sum_in_vif_type) AS deviation_from_avg_running_sum_in_vif_type FROM inner_cte ic JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON b.PORT_ID = ic.PORT_ID JOIN VifTypeStats vts ON vts.VIF_TYPE = b.VIF_TYPE ), tenant_down_secure_port_stats AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 ), TenantDownSecurePorts AS ( SELECT p.TENANT_ID, COUNT(*) AS down_secure_ports FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 GROUP BY p.TENANT_ID ), AverageDownSecurePorts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_secure_ports) AS avg_down_secure_ports FROM TenantDownSecurePorts ) SELECT tdsp.TENANT_ID, tdsp.down_secure_ports, adsp.avg_down_secure_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tdsp.down_secure_ports > adsp.avg_down_secure_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tdsp.down_secure_ports < adsp.avg_down_secure_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category, inner_cte.down_ports_with_port_security_enabled AS overall_down_secure_ports FROM TenantDownSecurePorts tdsp CROSS JOIN AverageDownSecurePorts adsp CROSS JOIN inner_cte ) SELECT pvrs.PORT_ID, pvrs.TENANT_ID, pvrs.MAC_ADDRESS, pvrs.running_sum_standard_attr_id, pvrs.ports_in_vif_type, pvrs.deviation_from_avg_running_sum_in_vif_type, tdsp.down_secure_ports, tdsp.benchmark, tdsp.user_category, tdsp.overall_down_secure_ports FROM port_vif_running_sums pvrs JOIN tenant_down_secure_port_stats tdsp ON tdsp.TENANT_ID = pvrs.TENANT_ID;

question: List the IPv4 subnet names that either have a DNS nameserver order coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) categorized as HIGH_VARIATION relative to the overall IPv4 benchmark, or have a DNS nameserver order range greater than the average order range across all IPv4 subnets, along with the reason for inclusion. Do not return any rounded answers. Categorize each subnet as 'HIGH_VARIATION' (at least 50% higher than the benchmark), 'LOW_VARIATION' (at least 50% lower than the benchmark), or 'AVERAGE_VARIATION'.
SQL: WITH CoeffVariationSubnets AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, STDDEV(d.ORDER) / NULLIF(AVG(d.ORDER), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s.id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name HAVING AVG(d.ORDER) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC), AvgCoeff AS ( SELECT AVG(coefficient_of_variation) AS avg_coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.subnet_name, i.coefficient_of_variation, a.avg_coefficient_of_variation AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.coefficient_of_variation > a.avg_coefficient_of_variation * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_VARIATION' WHEN i.coefficient_of_variation < a.avg_coefficient_of_variation * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_VARIATION' ELSE 'AVERAGE_VARIATION' END AS variation_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN AvgCoeff a ORDER BY i.coefficient_of_variation DESC), HighRangeSubnets AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(d.ORDER) - MIN(d.ORDER) AS order_range, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.id = d.subnet_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY order_range DESC) SELECT subnet_name, order_range, order_variance FROM inner_cte WHERE order_range > (SELECT AVG(order_range) FROM inner_cte) ORDER BY order_range DESC), CombinedSubnetFindings AS ( SELECT subnet_name, 'High Coefficient of Variation vs Benchmark' AS reason FROM CoeffVariationSubnets WHERE variation_category = 'HIGH_VARIATION' UNION ALL SELECT subnet_name, 'Order Range Above IPv4 Average' AS reason FROM HighRangeSubnets ) SELECT subnet_name, reason FROM CombinedSubnetFindings ORDER BY subnet_name, reason;

question: For DOWN-status ports on host "drive-59", show the port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, the row number ordered by IP address (with a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row), the total number of DOWN-port IP allocations per host and each row’s deviation from the average across hosts, along with the port MAC address and the running sum of port standard attribute IDs within each VIF type group. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), HostCounts AS ( SELECT host, COUNT(DISTINCT ip_address) AS down_allocated_ips FROM inner_cte GROUP BY host ), AverageHostCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_allocated_ips) AS avg_down_allocated_ips FROM HostCounts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.window_column, hc.down_allocated_ips, (hc.down_allocated_ips - ahc.avg_down_allocated_ips) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i JOIN HostCounts hc ON i.host = hc.host CROSS JOIN AverageHostCounts ahc ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(vif_type) OVER (ORDER BY vif_type_sort, vif_type, standard_attr_id, port_id) = vif_type THEN NULL ELSE vif_type END AS vif_type, port_id, tenant_id, mac_address, running_sum_standard_attr_ids FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(b.vif_type) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE b.vif_type END AS vif_type_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(b.vif_type) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE b.vif_type END AS vif_type, i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, p.standard_attr_id, i.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_ids FROM inner_cte i JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON b.port_id = i.port_id JOIN PORTS p ON p.id = i.port_id GROUP BY b.vif_type, i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, p.standard_attr_id, i.window_column WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY vif_type_sort, vif_type, standard_attr_id, port_id ) SELECT q1.port_id, q1.tenant_id, q1.host, q1.vif_type, q1.ip_address, q1.window_column AS down_port_ip_row_number, q1.down_allocated_ips, q1.deviation_from_avg, q2.mac_address, q2.running_sum_standard_attr_ids FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q1.port_id = q2.port_id WHERE q1.host = 'drive-59';

question: List port-status insights by combining (1) a rollup of port counts and earliest standard-attribute update timestamps per port status and device owner for ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports' (including subtotals and a grand total) and (2) per-status variance of STANDARD_ATTR_ID for ports that have an IP allocation, including the overall average variance benchmark and a variance category, and label each row with the reason it appears. Do not return any rounded answers. Categorize each status as 'HIGH_VARIANCE' (at least 50% above the benchmark), 'LOW_VARIANCE' (at least 50% below the benchmark), or 'AVERAGE_VARIANCE'.
SQL: WITH PortStatusOwnerRollup AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(port_status) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE port_status END AS port_status, CASE WHEN GROUPING(device_owner) = 1 AND GROUPING(port_status) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE device_owner END AS device_owner, SUM(port_count) AS port_count, MIN(earliest_standard_attr_update) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM inner_cte GROUP BY port_status, device_owner WITH ROLLUP ), PortStatusVariance AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.STATUS, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM PORTS AS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.STATUS ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC), AverageVariance AS ( SELECT AVG(standard_attr_id_variance) AS avg_variance FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.STATUS, i.standard_attr_id_variance, av.avg_variance AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.standard_attr_id_variance > av.avg_variance * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_VARIANCE' WHEN i.standard_attr_id_variance < av.avg_variance * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_VARIANCE' ELSE 'AVERAGE_VARIANCE' END AS variance_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN AverageVariance av ), CombinedStatusInsights AS ( SELECT psor.port_status AS port_status, psor.device_owner AS device_owner, psor.port_count AS port_count, psor.earliest_standard_attr_update AS earliest_standard_attr_update, NULL AS standard_attr_id_variance, NULL AS benchmark, NULL AS variance_category, 'Port Count Rollup' AS reason FROM PortStatusOwnerRollup psor UNION ALL SELECT psv.STATUS AS port_status, NULL AS device_owner, NULL AS port_count, NULL AS earliest_standard_attr_update, psv.standard_attr_id_variance AS standard_attr_id_variance, psv.benchmark AS benchmark, psv.variance_category AS variance_category, 'Standard Attr ID Variance (IP Allocations)' AS reason FROM PortStatusVariance psv ) SELECT * FROM CombinedStatusInsights ORDER BY port_status, reason, device_owner;

question: For ports that are DOWN and appear in both the ML2 port bindings and security-group bindings views, list each port’s ID, name, tenant ID, MAC address, admin_state_up flag, binding host, and VIF type; also include (1) the average admin_state_up over a window of 2 preceding and 2 following rows within each VIF type ordered by MAC address, along with the DOWN-port count per VIF type and its deviation from the overall average across VIF types, and (2) the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within each security group plus the tenant’s total DOWN-port count, the average DOWN-port count across tenants as a benchmark, and the tenant category (HIGH_USER/LOW_USER/AVERAGE_USER). Do not return any rounded answers. Categorize each tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), VifTypeCounts AS ( SELECT VIF_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_in_vif_type FROM inner_cte GROUP BY VIF_TYPE ), AverageVifTypeCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_ports_in_vif_type) AS avg_down_ports_per_vif_type FROM VifTypeCounts ) SELECT i.NAME, i.MAC_ADDRESS, i.ADMIN_STATE_UP, i.HOST, i.VIF_TYPE, i.window_column, vtc.down_ports_in_vif_type, (vtc.down_ports_in_vif_type - avc.avg_down_ports_per_vif_type) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i JOIN VifTypeCounts vtc ON i.VIF_TYPE = vtc.VIF_TYPE CROSS JOIN AverageVifTypeCounts avc ORDER BY i.MAC_ADDRESS ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), TenantDownPorts AS ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT port_id) AS total_down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ), AverageDownPorts AS ( SELECT AVG(total_down_ports) AS avg_down_ports FROM TenantDownPorts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.window_column, tdp.total_down_ports, adp.avg_down_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tdp.total_down_ports > adp.avg_down_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tdp.total_down_ports < adp.avg_down_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM inner_cte i JOIN TenantDownPorts tdp ON i.tenant_id = tdp.tenant_id CROSS JOIN AverageDownPorts adp ) SELECT q2.port_id, q1.NAME AS port_name, q2.tenant_id, q1.MAC_ADDRESS, q1.ADMIN_STATE_UP, q1.HOST AS binding_host, q1.VIF_TYPE, q1.window_column AS avg_admin_state_up_window_2_pre_2_fol_by_vif, q1.down_ports_in_vif_type, q1.deviation_from_avg AS vif_type_down_port_count_deviation_from_avg, q2.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_security_group, q2.total_down_ports AS tenant_total_down_ports, q2.benchmark AS avg_down_ports_across_tenants_benchmark, q2.user_category AS tenant_user_category FROM q2 JOIN q1 ON q2.mac_address = q1.MAC_ADDRESS ORDER BY q1.MAC_ADDRESS;

question: For allowed address pairs on port ID `25d421c1-c76d-4c26-9550-9f871a1d5034`, list each allowed address pair’s MAC address and IP address along with the port ID and its bound security group ID, the running average of the port’s standard attribute ID (partitioned by port and ordered by allowed address pair IP) and its deviation from the overall average running average; also include, for that same security group, the range/variance/standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of allowed-address-pair counts per port (considering only ports with at least one allowed address pair), the security group’s average allowed-address-pair count per port, and that average’s deviation from the overall security-group average. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH sg_stats AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MAX(port_pair_count) - MIN(port_pair_count) AS pair_count_range, VARIANCE(port_pair_count) AS pair_count_variance, STDDEV(port_pair_count) AS pair_count_stddev FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS port_pair_count FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ALLOWEDADDRESSPAIRS AS aap ON p.ID = aap.PORT_ID GROUP BY p.ID ) AS port_stats ON sgpb.PORT_ID = port_stats.port_id GROUP BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY pair_count_range DESC ), SecurityGroupAverages AS ( SELECT sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS security_group_id, AVG(port_stats.port_pair_count) AS avg_pairs_per_port FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS port_pair_count FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ALLOWEDADDRESSPAIRS AS aap ON p.ID = aap.PORT_ID GROUP BY p.ID ) AS port_stats ON sgpb.PORT_ID = port_stats.port_id GROUP BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ), OverallAverage AS ( SELECT AVG(avg_pairs_per_port) AS overall_avg_pairs_per_port FROM SecurityGroupAverages ) SELECT i.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, i.pair_count_range, i.pair_count_variance, i.pair_count_stddev, sga.avg_pairs_per_port, (sga.avg_pairs_per_port - oa.overall_avg_pairs_per_port) AS deviation_from_overall_avg FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN SecurityGroupAverages AS sga ON i.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = sga.security_group_id CROSS JOIN OverallAverage AS oa ORDER BY i.pair_count_range DESC ), port_aap_stats AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT aap.MAC_ADDRESS AS allowed_mac_address, aap.IP_ADDRESS AS allowed_ip_address, p.ID AS port_id, sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS security_group_id, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY aap.IP_ADDRESS ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN ALLOWEDADDRESSPAIRS AS aap ON p.ID = aap.PORT_ID WHERE p.ID = '25d421c1-c76d-4c26-9550-9f871a1d5034' ORDER BY aap.IP_ADDRESS ), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(window_column) AS avg_window_column FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.allowed_mac_address, i.allowed_ip_address, i.port_id, i.security_group_id, i.window_column, (i.window_column - a.avg_window_column) AS deviation_from_avg_window FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a ORDER BY i.allowed_ip_address ) SELECT pas.allowed_mac_address, pas.allowed_ip_address, pas.port_id, pas.security_group_id, pas.window_column, pas.deviation_from_avg_window, sgs.pair_count_range, sgs.pair_count_variance, sgs.pair_count_stddev, sgs.avg_pairs_per_port, sgs.deviation_from_overall_avg FROM port_aap_stats AS pas JOIN sg_stats AS sgs ON pas.security_group_id = sgs.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY pas.allowed_ip_address;

question: For the RBAC action 'access_as_shared', show the action name, the average/variance/standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of subnet IP version across subnets on networks referenced by RBAC entries (restricted to IPv4 subnets), the overall average of these per-action average IP versions across all actions, and (for the same action) the total number of distinct referenced networks and total number of subnets on those referenced networks. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.ACTION, AVG(s.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance, STDDEV(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_stddev FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_variance DESC ) SELECT inner_cte.action, inner_cte.avg_ip_version, inner_cte.ip_version_variance, inner_cte.ip_version_stddev, overall_avg.avg_of_action_avg_ip_version FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(avg_ip_version) AS avg_of_action_avg_ip_version FROM inner_cte ) AS overall_avg ON 1 = 1 ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.ACTION, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_variance DESC ) SELECT i.ACTION, i.ip_version_variance, COUNT(DISTINCT n.OBJECT_ID) AS total_networks_referenced, COUNT(DISTINCT s.ID) AS total_subnets_on_referenced_networks FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON i.ACTION = n.ACTION JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY i.ACTION, i.ip_version_variance ORDER BY i.ip_version_variance DESC LIMIT 10 ) SELECT q1.action, q1.avg_ip_version, q1.ip_version_variance, q1.ip_version_stddev, q1.avg_of_action_avg_ip_version, q2.total_networks_referenced, q2.total_subnets_on_referenced_networks FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q1.action = q2.action WHERE q1.action = 'access_as_shared' ORDER BY q1.ip_version_variance DESC;

question: For each IPv4 subnet route that belongs to an ACTIVE network, list the route destination and next hop, the subnet name and CIDR, and the allocation pool first/last IP (keeping the dense-rank within each subnet), along with the subnet’s total route count, the overall average routes-per-IPv4-subnet benchmark and its route-category label; also include the active network’s ID, name, tenant ID, admin_state_up, MTU, standard-attribute updated_at timestamp, the row number of the network within its tenant (ordered by network name), the average MTU benchmark across active networks, and the network’s MTU category. Do not return any rounded answers. Classify each row’s subnet as 'HIGH_ROUTE_SUBNET' (at least 50% more routes than average), 'LOW_ROUTE_SUBNET' (at least 50% fewer routes than average), or 'AVERAGE_ROUTE_SUBNET'.
SQL: WITH RouteDetails AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT r.DESTINATION, r.NEXTHOP, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.SUBNET_ID ORDER BY r.SUBNET_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4), SubnetRouteCounts AS ( SELECT s.ID AS subnet_id, COUNT(r.DESTINATION) AS total_routes FROM SUBNETS s JOIN SUBNETROUTES r ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.ID ), AverageRoutes AS ( SELECT AVG(total_routes) AS avg_routes FROM SubnetRouteCounts ) SELECT i.DESTINATION, i.NEXTHOP, i.subnet_name, i.subnet_cidr, i.FIRST_IP, i.LAST_IP, i.window_column, src.total_routes, ar.avg_routes AS benchmark, CASE WHEN src.total_routes > ar.avg_routes * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_ROUTE_SUBNET' WHEN src.total_routes < ar.avg_routes * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_ROUTE_SUBNET' ELSE 'AVERAGE_ROUTE_SUBNET' END AS route_category FROM inner_cte i JOIN SUBNETS s ON s.CIDR = i.subnet_cidr AND s.NAME = i.subnet_name JOIN SubnetRouteCounts src ON src.subnet_id = s.ID CROSS JOIN AverageRoutes ar ), ActiveNetworkDetails AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE'), AvgMtu AS (SELECT AVG(mtu) AS avg_mtu FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.network_id, i.network_name, i.tenant_id, i.admin_state_up, i.mtu, i.standard_attr_updated_at, i.window_column, a.avg_mtu AS benchmark_avg_mtu, CASE WHEN i.mtu > a.avg_mtu THEN 'ABOVE_AVG_MTU' WHEN i.mtu < a.avg_mtu THEN 'BELOW_AVG_MTU' ELSE 'AT_AVG_MTU' END AS mtu_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN AvgMtu a ) SELECT rd.DESTINATION, rd.NEXTHOP, rd.subnet_name, rd.subnet_cidr, rd.FIRST_IP, rd.LAST_IP, rd.window_column AS subnet_dense_rank, rd.total_routes, rd.benchmark AS avg_routes_benchmark, rd.route_category, andt.network_id, andt.network_name, andt.tenant_id, andt.admin_state_up, andt.mtu, andt.standard_attr_updated_at, andt.window_column AS tenant_network_rownum, andt.benchmark_avg_mtu, andt.mtu_category FROM RouteDetails rd JOIN SUBNETS s ON s.CIDR = rd.subnet_cidr AND s.NAME = rd.subnet_name JOIN ActiveNetworkDetails andt ON andt.network_id = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ORDER BY andt.tenant_id, andt.network_name, rd.subnet_name, rd.DESTINATION;

question: For ports in status 'DOWN', list each port’s ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and the row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row). Also show, per host, the total number of DOWN-port IP allocations and each row’s deviation from the average DOWN-port IP allocations per host; and for the same tenant, include the tenant’s count of DOWN ports with port security enabled, the average of that count across tenants as a benchmark, the tenant’s usage category (HIGH_USER/LOW_USER/AVERAGE_USER), and the overall total number of DOWN ports with port security enabled. Do not return any rounded answers. Classify each tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), HostCounts AS ( SELECT host, COUNT(DISTINCT ip_address) AS down_allocated_ips FROM inner_cte GROUP BY host ), AverageHostCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_allocated_ips) AS avg_down_allocated_ips FROM HostCounts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.window_column, hc.down_allocated_ips, (hc.down_allocated_ips - ahc.avg_down_allocated_ips) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i JOIN HostCounts hc ON i.host = hc.host CROSS JOIN AverageHostCounts ahc ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 ), TenantDownSecurePorts AS ( SELECT p.TENANT_ID, COUNT(*) AS down_secure_ports FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 GROUP BY p.TENANT_ID ), AverageDownSecurePorts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_secure_ports) AS avg_down_secure_ports FROM TenantDownSecurePorts ) SELECT tdsp.TENANT_ID, tdsp.down_secure_ports, adsp.avg_down_secure_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tdsp.down_secure_ports > adsp.avg_down_secure_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tdsp.down_secure_ports < adsp.avg_down_secure_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category, inner_cte.down_ports_with_port_security_enabled AS overall_down_secure_ports FROM TenantDownSecurePorts tdsp CROSS JOIN AverageDownSecurePorts adsp CROSS JOIN inner_cte ) SELECT q1.port_id, q1.tenant_id, q1.host, q1.vif_type, q1.ip_address, q1.window_column, q1.down_allocated_ips, q1.deviation_from_avg, q2.down_secure_ports, q2.benchmark AS avg_down_secure_ports_benchmark, q2.user_category, q2.overall_down_secure_ports FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q1.tenant_id = q2.tenant_id ORDER BY q1.host, q1.ip_address;

question: For DOWN ports that belong to ACTIVE networks, list each port’s ID, port tenant ID, port name, network ID, network name, network tenant ID, admin_state_up, MTU, the network standard attribute updated_at timestamp, the row number of the network within its tenant (ordered by network name), the average MTU across all active networks and the network’s MTU category versus that average, plus the port MAC address, device owner, allocated IP address, the row number of the port within its network (ordered by port ID), and for that network the total number of DOWN port IP allocations and the deviation of that total from the average across all networks. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH down_ports AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), NetworkDownAllocations AS ( SELECT network_id, COUNT(DISTINCT ip_address) AS down_allocated_ips FROM inner_cte GROUP BY network_id ), AverageNetworkDownAllocations AS ( SELECT AVG(down_allocated_ips) AS avg_down_allocated_ips FROM NetworkDownAllocations ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.port_name, i.network_id, i.mac_address, i.device_owner, i.ip_address, i.window_column, nda.down_allocated_ips, (nda.down_allocated_ips - anda.avg_down_allocated_ips) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i JOIN NetworkDownAllocations nda ON i.network_id = nda.network_id CROSS JOIN AverageNetworkDownAllocations anda ), active_networks AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE'), AvgMtu AS (SELECT AVG(mtu) AS avg_mtu FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.network_id, i.network_name, i.tenant_id, i.admin_state_up, i.mtu, i.standard_attr_updated_at, i.window_column, a.avg_mtu AS benchmark_avg_mtu, CASE WHEN i.mtu > a.avg_mtu THEN 'ABOVE_AVG_MTU' WHEN i.mtu < a.avg_mtu THEN 'BELOW_AVG_MTU' ELSE 'AT_AVG_MTU' END AS mtu_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN AvgMtu a ) SELECT dp.port_id, dp.tenant_id AS port_tenant_id, dp.port_name, dp.network_id, an.network_name, an.tenant_id AS network_tenant_id, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at, an.window_column AS network_rownum_within_tenant, an.benchmark_avg_mtu, an.mtu_category, dp.mac_address, dp.device_owner, dp.ip_address, dp.window_column AS port_rownum_within_network, dp.down_allocated_ips, dp.deviation_from_avg FROM down_ports dp JOIN active_networks an ON dp.network_id = an.network_id;

question: Return the port status/device-owner rollup for ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports' (including the port count and earliest standard-attribute updated timestamp), and alongside it also return overall tenant-level totals for administratively up ports that have at least one IP allocation (total such ports, total IP allocations, total subnet-id rows, and the average number of such ports per tenant across all tenants). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH PortStatusOwnerRollup AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(port_status) OVER (ORDER BY port_status_sort, port_status, device_owner) = port_status THEN NULL ELSE port_status END AS port_status, device_owner, port_count, earliest_standard_attr_update FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.port_status) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE i.port_status END AS port_status_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.port_status) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE i.port_status END AS port_status, i.device_owner AS device_owner, SUM(i.port_count) AS port_count, MIN(i.earliest_standard_attr_update) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM inner_cte i GROUP BY i.port_status, i.device_owner WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp
