route_stats.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 AND s.ID IN ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48') GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY route_count_range DESC), SubnetTenantStats AS ( SELECT s.tenant_id, i.subnet_name, i.route_count_range, i.route_count_variance, i.route_count_stddev FROM inner_cte i JOIN subnets s ON s.name = i.subnet_name AND s.ip_version = 4 AND s.id IN ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48') ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(tenant_id) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE tenant_id END AS tenant_id, CASE WHEN GROUPING(subnet_name) = 1 AND GROUPING(tenant_id) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' WHEN GROUPING(subnet_name) = 1 AND GROUPING(tenant_id) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE subnet_name END AS subnet_name, AVG(route_count_range) AS avg_route_count_range, AVG(route_count_variance) AS avg_route_count_variance, AVG(route_count_stddev) AS avg_route_count_stddev FROM SubnetTenantStats GROUP BY tenant_id, subnet_name WITH ROLLUP ), top10_subnets_by_distinct_routes AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT r.DESTINATION, r.NEXTHOP, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.SUBNET_ID ORDER BY r.SUBNET_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 AND s.ID IN ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48')) SELECT s.ID AS subnet_id, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, COUNT(DISTINCT r.DESTINATION) AS total_routes, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_allocation_pools FROM SUBNETS s LEFT JOIN SUBNETROUTES r ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID LEFT JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON p.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN inner_cte i ON i.subnet_name = s.NAME AND i.subnet_cidr = s.CIDR WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 AND s.ID IN ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48') GROUP BY s.ID, s.NAME, s.CIDR ORDER BY total_routes DESC LIMIT 10 ) SELECT t.subnet_id, t.subnet_name, t.subnet_cidr, t.total_routes, t.has_allocation_pools, d.tenant_id, d.avg_route_count_range, d.avg_route_count_variance, d.avg_route_count_stddev FROM top10_subnets_by_distinct_routes t JOIN subnet_route_dispersion d ON d.subnet_name = t.subnet_name WHERE d.subnet_name <> 'SUBTOTAL' AND d.tenant_id <> 'GRAND TOTAL';

question: For ports that are administratively up, list the VIF type, total number of distinct ports, and the average of the per-port windowed average standard attribute ID (computed over 2 preceding and 2 following rows partitioned by VIF type and ordered by standard attribute ID). Do not repeat the VIF type if it is the same as the previous row. Include a grand total row across all VIF types. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, b.VNIC_TYPE, p.TENANT_ID, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(vif_type) OVER (ORDER BY vif_type_sort, vif_type) = vif_type THEN NULL ELSE vif_type END AS vif_type, total_ports, avg_windowed_standard_attr_id FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.VIF_TYPE) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE i.VIF_TYPE END AS vif_type_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.VIF_TYPE) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE i.VIF_TYPE END AS vif_type, COUNT(DISTINCT i.PORT_ID) AS total_ports, AVG(i.window_column) AS avg_windowed_standard_attr_id FROM inner_cte AS i GROUP BY i.VIF_TYPE WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY vif_type_sort, vif_type;

question: For each tenant that has ports in DOWN status, list the tenant ID, the total number of DOWN ports they have (based on the DOWN ports joined to their security-group-to-port bindings and port-security bindings), and the average number of DOWN ports per tenant across all such tenants. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' ) SELECT inner_cte.tenant_id, COUNT(inner_cte.port_id) AS total_down_ports, avg_down.avg_down_port_count FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_port_count FROM ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(port_id) AS down_port_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS sub ) AS avg_down GROUP BY inner_cte.tenant_id, avg_down.avg_down_port_count;

question: For load balancers provided by “haproxy”, list the load balancer name, VIP address, bytes in, total connections, and the row number ordered by load balancer name using a window frame of 2 preceding and 1 following rows; additionally, for each tenant show how many haproxy load balancers they have and the average number of haproxy load balancers per tenant. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT lb.NAME AS loadbalancer_name, lb.VIP_ADDRESS AS vip_address, stats.BYTES_IN AS bytes_in, stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS AS total_connections, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY lb.NAME ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb ON stats.LOADBALANCER_ID = lb.ID JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' ) SELECT inner_cte.loadbalancer_name, inner_cte.vip_address, inner_cte.bytes_in, inner_cte.total_connections, inner_cte.window_column, lb.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, tenant_counts.haproxy_lb_count AS tenant_haproxy_loadbalancer_count, avg_counts.avg_haproxy_lb_count AS avg_haproxy_loadbalancers_per_tenant FROM inner_cte JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb ON lb.NAME = inner_cte.loadbalancer_name AND lb.VIP_ADDRESS = inner_cte.vip_address JOIN ( SELECT lb2.TENANT_ID, COUNT(lb2.ID) AS haproxy_lb_count FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb2 JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra2 ON lb2.ID = pra2.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra2.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' GROUP BY lb2.TENANT_ID ) AS tenant_counts ON tenant_counts.TENANT_ID = lb.TENANT_ID JOIN ( SELECT AVG(sub.haproxy_lb_count) AS avg_haproxy_lb_count FROM ( SELECT lb3.TENANT_ID, COUNT(lb3.ID) AS haproxy_lb_count FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb3 JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra3 ON lb3.ID = pra3.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra3.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' GROUP BY lb3.TENANT_ID ) AS sub ) AS avg_counts ON 1 = 1;

question: Among the top 10 tenants with the highest number of ACTIVE networks that have an RBAC rule with action 'access_as_shared', show each tenant's ID, the total number of such networks, and whether any of those networks are shared to at least one specific target tenant (i.e., TARGET_TENANT is not '*'). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS active_shared_rbac_networks FROM NETWORKS n JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.ID = r.OBJECT_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' AND r.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ) SELECT n.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT n.id) AS total_active_shared_networks, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN r.target_tenant <> '*' THEN r.id END) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_specific_target_tenant_share FROM NETWORKS n JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.ID = r.OBJECT_ID CROSS JOIN inner_cte WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' AND r.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.tenant_id ORDER BY total_active_shared_networks DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For each network status, show the status, the variance and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the security group binding order (PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) across networks that have at least one security binding, and also include the overall average of these per-status variances across all statuses. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.STATUS AS network_status, VARIANCE(nsb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) AS port_security_enabled_variance, STDDEV(nsb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) AS port_security_enabled_stddev FROM NETWORKS AS n JOIN NETWORKSECURITYBINDINGS AS nsb ON n.ID = nsb.NETWORK_ID GROUP BY n.STATUS ORDER BY port_security_enabled_variance DESC ) SELECT inner_cte.network_status, inner_cte.port_security_enabled_variance, inner_cte.port_security_enabled_stddev, avg_vars.avg_variance_across_statuses FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(port_security_enabled_variance) AS avg_variance_across_statuses FROM inner_cte ) AS avg_vars ORDER BY inner_cte.port_security_enabled_variance DESC;

question: For ports that are DOWN, show the port name, MAC address, admin_state_up flag, binding host, VIF type, and the average admin_state_up in a window of 2 preceding and 2 following rows partitioned by VIF type and ordered by MAC address. Also include, for each VIF type, a subtotal row with the total number of DOWN ports and the average of the windowed admin_state_up values, and do not repeat the VIF type if it is the same as the previous row. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(vif_type) OVER (ORDER BY vif_type_sort, vif_type, mac_address) = vif_type THEN NULL ELSE vif_type END AS vif_type, name, mac_address, admin_state_up, host, window_column, down_ports_count, avg_window_column FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.vif_type) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE i.vif_type END AS vif_type_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.vif_type) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE i.vif_type END AS vif_type, i.name, i.mac_address, i.admin_state_up, i.host, i.window_column, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_count, AVG(i.window_column) AS avg_window_column FROM inner_cte AS i GROUP BY i.vif_type, i.name, i.mac_address, i.admin_state_up, i.host, i.window_column WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY vif_type_sort, vif_type, mac_address;

question: For IPv4 subnets whose DNS nameserver order values are highly variable (coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) greater than 0.5), list the subnet name, the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of DNS nameserver order values, and the number of IP allocation pools on that subnet. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, STDDEV(d.ORDER) / NULLIF(AVG(d.ORDER), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s.id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name HAVING AVG(d.ORDER) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC) SELECT inner_cte.subnet_name, inner_cte.coefficient_of_variation, COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS ip_allocation_pool_count FROM inner_cte JOIN subnets s ON s.name = inner_cte.subnet_name JOIN ipallocationpools p ON p.subnet_id = s.id WHERE inner_cte.coefficient_of_variation > 0.5 GROUP BY inner_cte.subnet_name, inner_cte.coefficient_of_variation ORDER BY inner_cte.coefficient_of_variation DESC;

question: For each load balancer operating status, show the operating status and the total incoming bytes across load balancers that are in ACTIVE provisioning status, keeping only operating statuses where the total incoming bytes exceed 1,000,000. Also include subtotals per operating status and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT lb.OPERATING_STATUS, SUM(s.BYTES_IN) AS total_bytes_in FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS s ON lb.ID = s.LOADBALANCER_ID WHERE lb.PROVISIONING_STATUS = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY lb.OPERATING_STATUS HAVING SUM(s.BYTES_IN) > 1000000 ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(OPERATING_STATUS) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE OPERATING_STATUS END AS OPERATING_STATUS, SUM(total_bytes_in) AS total_bytes_in FROM inner_cte GROUP BY OPERATING_STATUS WITH ROLLUP;

question: For each administratively up port that has at least one IP allocation, list the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the number of IP allocations on that port, and the number of subnet-id rows. Do not repeat the tenant ID if it is the same as the previous row. Also include a subtotal row per tenant and a grand total row. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ia.subnet_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS subnet_id_rows FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(tenant_id) OVER (ORDER BY tenant_id_sort, tenant_id, port_id) = tenant_id THEN NULL ELSE tenant_id END AS tenant_id, port_id, mac_address, ip_allocation_count, subnet_id_rows FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(inner_cte.tenant_id) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE inner_cte.tenant_id END AS tenant_id_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(inner_cte.tenant_id) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE inner_cte.tenant_id END AS tenant_id, CASE WHEN GROUPING(inner_cte.port_id) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE inner_cte.port_id END AS port_id, CASE WHEN GROUPING(inner_cte.port_id) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE inner_cte.mac_address END AS mac_address, SUM(inner_cte.ip_allocation_count) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(inner_cte.subnet_id_rows) AS subnet_id_rows FROM inner_cte GROUP BY inner_cte.tenant_id, inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.mac_address WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY tenant_id_sort, tenant_id, port_id;

question: For each tenant, list the tenant ID and the number of load balancers that are ONLINE and associated with the provider named 'haproxy', but only include tenants whose count is greater than the average such count across all tenants. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS online_haproxy_loadbalancers FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS lb JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE lb.OPERATING_STATUS = 'ONLINE' AND pra.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' ), TenantCounts AS ( SELECT lb.TENANT_ID, COUNT(*) AS tenant_online_haproxy_count FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS lb JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE lb.OPERATING_STATUS = 'ONLINE' AND pra.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' GROUP BY lb.TENANT_ID ), AvgTenantCount AS ( SELECT AVG(tenant_online_haproxy_count) AS avg_tenant_online_haproxy_count FROM TenantCounts ) SELECT tc.TENANT_ID, tc.tenant_online_haproxy_count FROM TenantCounts tc CROSS JOIN inner_cte CROSS JOIN AvgTenantCount atc WHERE tc.tenant_online_haproxy_count > atc.avg_tenant_online_haproxy_count;

question: For each ACTIVE network, show the network name and the maximum total number of security bindings found among networks that have more than 1 security binding in total. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.name AS network_name, SUM(1) AS total_security_bindings FROM NETWORKS n JOIN NETWORKSECURITYBINDINGS nsb ON n.id = nsb.network_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n.name HAVING SUM(1) > 1) SELECT MAX(total_security_bindings) AS max_total_security_bindings FROM inner_cte;

question: For allowed address pairs on the port with ID `25d421c1-c76d-4c26-9550-9f871a1d5034`, show the allowed address pair MAC address, allowed address pair IP address, the port ID, the security group ID bound to that port, the running average of the port’s standard attribute ID within each port (partitioned by port ID) ordered by the allowed address pair IP address, and the deviation of that running average from the overall average running average across the returned rows. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT aap.MAC_ADDRESS AS allowed_mac_address, aap.IP_ADDRESS AS allowed_ip_address, p.ID AS port_id, sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS security_group_id, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY aap.IP_ADDRESS ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN ALLOWEDADDRESSPAIRS AS aap ON p.ID = aap.PORT_ID WHERE p.ID = '25d421c1-c76d-4c26-9550-9f871a1d5034' ORDER BY aap.IP_ADDRESS ), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(window_column) AS avg_window_column FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.allowed_mac_address, i.allowed_ip_address, i.port_id, i.security_group_id, i.window_column, (i.window_column - a.avg_window_column) AS deviation_from_avg_window FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a ORDER BY i.allowed_ip_address;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, show the port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and the row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row). Also include, for each host, the total number of such DOWN-port IP allocations and the deviation of each row from the average number of DOWN-port IP allocations per host. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), HostCounts AS ( SELECT host, COUNT(DISTINCT ip_address) AS down_allocated_ips FROM inner_cte GROUP BY host ), AverageHostCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_allocated_ips) AS avg_down_allocated_ips FROM HostCounts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.window_column, hc.down_allocated_ips, (hc.down_allocated_ips - ahc.avg_down_allocated_ips) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i JOIN HostCounts hc ON i.host = hc.host CROSS JOIN AverageHostCounts ahc;

question: For each port status and host, list the port status, the host name, and the number of host/status groups returned by the query for ports that have an allowed address pair with IP address 10.232.210.41/8 and whose highest port standard attribute ID (within each host/status group) is greater than 1. Include subtotals per port status and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT b.HOST, MAX(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS max_standard_attr_id, p.STATUS FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN ALLOWEDADDRESSPAIRS a ON p.ID = a.PORT_ID WHERE a.IP_ADDRESS = '10.232.210.41/8' GROUP BY b.HOST, p.STATUS HAVING MAX(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) > 1 ), HostStatusCounts AS ( SELECT status, host, COUNT(*) AS total_groups FROM inner_cte GROUP BY status, host ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(status) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE status END AS status, CASE WHEN GROUPING(host) = 1 AND GROUPING(status) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE host END AS host, SUM(total_groups) AS total_groups FROM HostStatusCounts GROUP BY status, host WITH ROLLUP;

question: For each port status, list the port status, an IP-allocation category ('Has IP Allocation' if the status has any ports with an IP allocation, 'No IP Allocation' otherwise), and the variance of the standard attribute ID across ports that have an IP allocation. Include subtotals per port status and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.STATUS, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM PORTS AS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.STATUS ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC), PortStatusAlloc AS ( SELECT p.status, CASE WHEN ia.port_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'Has IP Allocation' ELSE 'No IP Allocation' END AS ip_allocation_status, VARIANCE(p.standard_attr_id) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM ports p LEFT JOIN ipallocations ia ON p.id = ia.port_id WHERE p.standard_attr_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.status, ip_allocation_status ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(psa.status) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE psa.status END AS status, CASE WHEN GROUPING(psa.ip_allocation_status) = 1 AND GROUPING(psa.status) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE psa.ip_allocation_status END AS ip_allocation_status, SUM(psa.standard_attr_id_variance) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM PortStatusAlloc psa JOIN inner_cte i ON i.status = psa.status GROUP BY psa.status, psa.ip_allocation_status WITH ROLLUP;

question: For DOWN ports, show the port ID, port name, MAC address, binding host, VIF type, and the rank of each port within its status group ordered by port ID. Also include the number of DOWN ports per binding host and VIF type, with subtotals per host and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), PortCounts AS ( SELECT binding_host, vif_type, COUNT(DISTINCT port_id) AS total_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY binding_host, vif_type ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(binding_host) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE binding_host END AS binding_host, CASE WHEN GROUPING(vif_type) = 1 AND GROUPING(binding_host) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE vif_type END AS vif_type, SUM(total_ports) AS total_ports FROM PortCounts GROUP BY binding_host, vif_type WITH ROLLUP;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, show the port ID, port name, MAC address, the binding host, VIF type, and the rank of each port within its status group ordered by port ID. Do not repeat the binding host if it is the same as the previous row, and include subtotals for each VIF type. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(binding_host) OVER (ORDER BY vif_type_sort, vif_type, port_id) = binding_host THEN NULL ELSE binding_host END AS binding_host, port_id, port_name, mac_address, vif_type, window_column FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(vif_type) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE vif_type END AS vif_type_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(vif_type) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE vif_type END AS vif_type, port_id, port_name, mac_address, binding_host, window_column FROM inner_cte GROUP BY vif_type, port_id, port_name, mac_address, binding_host, window_column WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY vif_type_sort, vif_type, port_id;

question: For ACTIVE networks, show the network name, status, and admin_state_up along with the RBAC action and target tenant, but only return those networks whose number of RBAC entries is greater than the average RBAC-entry count across all ACTIVE networks. Also include a dense rank within each network (partitioned by network ID and ordered by network ID). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.name, n.status, n.admin_state_up, r.action, r.target_tenant, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY n.id ORDER BY n.id) AS window_column FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' ), NetworkRbacCounts AS ( SELECT n.id AS network_id, COUNT(r.id) AS total_rbacs FROM networks n JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n.id ) SELECT i.name, i.status, i.admin_state_up, i.action, i.target_tenant, i.window_column FROM inner_cte i JOIN networks n ON n.name = i.name AND n.status = i.status AND n.admin_state_up = i.admin_state_up JOIN NetworkRbacCounts c ON c.network_id = n.id WHERE c.total_rbacs > (SELECT AVG(total_rbacs) FROM NetworkRbacCounts);

question: For ports that are DOWN, list the port name, network ID, MAC address, admin state, status, device owner, bound security group ID, and the minimum admin_state_up value in a window of 3 preceding and 1 following row ordered by port ID, but only include security groups that are bound to more than 5 DOWN ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT NAME, NETWORK_ID, MAC_ADDRESS, ADMIN_STATE_UP, STATUS, DEVICE_OWNER, SECURITY_GROUP_ID, window_column FROM inner_cte WHERE SECURITY_GROUP_ID IN (SELECT SECURITY_GROUP_ID FROM inner_cte GROUP BY SECURITY_GROUP_ID HAVING COUNT(*) > 5);

question: For each network, show the network ID and the maximum geometric mean of the standard attribute IDs (considering only standard attribute IDs greater than 0) among all security groups that have ports in that network. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, EXP(AVG(LN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID))) AS geometric_mean_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID > 0 GROUP BY s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY geometric_mean_standard_attr_id DESC ), NetworkSecurityGroupGeoMean AS ( SELECT p.NETWORK_ID, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, i.geometric_mean_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID JOIN inner_cte AS i ON i.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ) SELECT NETWORK_ID, MAX(geometric_mean_standard_attr_id) AS max_security_group_geometric_mean_standard_attr_id FROM NetworkSecurityGroupGeoMean GROUP BY NETWORK_ID;

question: For networks that have more ports in status 'DOWN' with port security enabled than the average across all networks, list the network ID and the total number of such ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 ), NetworkDownSecurePorts AS ( SELECT p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, COUNT(*) AS total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 GROUP BY p.NETWORK_ID ) SELECT network_id, total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM NetworkDownSecurePorts WHERE total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled > ( SELECT AVG(total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled) FROM NetworkDownSecurePorts );

question: For load balancers provided by the “haproxy” provider, list the provider name, load balancer name, load balancer ID, VIP address, provisioning status, operating status, and the running average of the load balancer ID within each provider name group ordered by load balancer name. Do not repeat the provider name if it is the same as the previous row, and include a subtotal row for the provider. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT lb.NAME, lb.ID, lb.VIP_ADDRESS, lb.PROVISIONING_STATUS, lb.OPERATING_STATUS, AVG(lb.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY pra.PROVIDER_NAME ORDER BY lb.NAME ) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(provider_name) OVER (ORDER BY provider_name_sort, lb_name) = provider_name THEN NULL ELSE provider_name END AS provider_name, lb_name, lb_id, vip_address, provisioning_status, operating_status, window_column FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(pra.PROVIDER_NAME) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE pra.PROVIDER_NAME END AS provider_name_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(pra.PROVIDER_NAME) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE pra.PROVIDER_NAME END AS provider_name, inner_cte.NAME AS lb_name, inner_cte.ID AS lb_id, inner_cte.VIP_ADDRESS AS vip_address, inner_cte.PROVISIONING_STATUS AS provisioning_status, inner_cte.OPERATING_STATUS AS operating_status, inner_cte.window_column AS window_column FROM inner_cte JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON inner_cte.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID GROUP BY pra.PROVIDER_NAME, inner_cte.NAME, inner_cte.ID, inner_cte.VIP_ADDRESS, inner_cte.PROVISIONING_STATUS, inner_cte.OPERATING_STATUS, inner_cte.window_column WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY provider_name_sort, lb_name;

question: For each administratively up port, list the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the number of port security bindings on that port, the total number of times port security is enabled across those bindings, and the deviation of that enabled total from the average enabled total across all administratively up ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(port_security_enabled_total) AS avg_enabled_total FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.binding_count, i.port_security_enabled_total, (i.port_security_enabled_total - a.avg_enabled_total) AS deviation_from_avg_enabled_total FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a;

question: For subnets whose network has a RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', return only those subnets whose running sum of standard attribute IDs (within each IP version group ordered by standard attribute ID) is greater than the average running sum across all such subnets; list the subnet name, its CIDR, the RBAC target tenant, and the running sum. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ) SELECT subnet_name, subnet_cidr, rbac_target_tenant, window_column FROM inner_cte WHERE window_column > (SELECT AVG(window_column) FROM inner_cte);

question: For each port status, list the status, the minimum admin_state_up value, and the average standard_attr_id for ports bound with VIF type 'ovs', but only include statuses where the average standard_attr_id is greater than the overall average standard_attr_id across all 'ovs' bound ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) AS min_admin_state_up, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS avg_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE b.VIF_TYPE = 'ovs' GROUP BY p.STATUS) SELECT p.STATUS, inner_cte.min_admin_state_up, inner_cte.avg_standard_attr_id FROM inner_cte JOIN PORTS p ON 1 = 1 JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE b.VIF_TYPE = 'ovs' GROUP BY p.STATUS, inner_cte.min_admin_state_up, inner_cte.avg_standard_attr_id HAVING inner_cte.avg_standard_attr_id > (SELECT AVG(p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) FROM PORTS p2 JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b2 ON p2.ID = b2.PORT_ID WHERE b2.VIF_TYPE = 'ovs');

question: For each tenant, report the number of ports that are in status 'DOWN' and have port security enabled, the average of that count across all tenants as a benchmark, and classify each tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 ), TenantDownSecurePorts AS ( SELECT p.TENANT_ID, COUNT(*) AS down_secure_ports FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 GROUP BY p.TENANT_ID ), AverageDownSecurePorts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_secure_ports) AS avg_down_secure_ports FROM TenantDownSecurePorts ) SELECT tdsp.TENANT_ID, tdsp.down_secure_ports, adsp.avg_down_secure_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tdsp.down_secure_ports > adsp.avg_down_secure_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tdsp.down_secure_ports < adsp.avg_down_secure_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category, inner_cte.down_ports_with_port_security_enabled AS overall_down_secure_ports FROM TenantDownSecurePorts tdsp CROSS JOIN AverageDownSecurePorts adsp CROSS JOIN inner_cte;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, list the port ID, tenant ID, and MAC address, along with the running sum of the standard attribute IDs within each resource type group ordered by standard attribute ID, but only include ports whose standard attribute ID is above the average standard attribute ID for DOWN ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.tenant_id, inner_cte.mac_address, inner_cte.window_column FROM inner_cte JOIN PORTS p2 ON p2.ID = inner_cte.port_id JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa2 ON sa2.ID = p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa2.ID > (SELECT AVG(sa3.ID) FROM PORTS p3 JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa3 ON sa3.ID = p3.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p3.STATUS = 'DOWN');

question: For each subnet IP version and DHCP status (label DHCP as 'DHCP Enabled' when enable_dhcp = 1, otherwise 'DHCP Disabled'), show the range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the number of IP allocation pools per subnet, considering only subnets that have at least one DNS nameserver entry. Include subtotals per IP version and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(pool_count) - MIN(pool_count) AS pool_count_range, VARIANCE(pool_count) AS pool_count_variance, STDDEV(pool_count) AS pool_count_stddev FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ( SELECT s2.id AS subnet_id, COUNT(*) AS pool_count FROM subnets AS s2 JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s2.id GROUP BY s2.id, p.id ) AS pool_stats ON pool_stats.subnet_id = s.id GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY pool_count_range DESC ), SubnetDims AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, s.ip_version, CASE WHEN s.enable_dhcp = 1 THEN 'DHCP Enabled' ELSE 'DHCP Disabled' END AS dhcp_status FROM subnets s JOIN dnsnameservers d ON d.subnet_id = s.id ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(sd.ip_version) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE CAST(sd.ip_version AS CHAR) END AS ip_version, CASE WHEN GROUPING(sd.dhcp_status) = 1 AND GROUPING(sd.ip_version) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE sd.dhcp_status END AS dhcp_status, MAX(ic.pool_count_range) AS pool_count_range, AVG(ic.pool_count_variance) AS pool_count_variance, AVG(ic.pool_count_stddev) AS pool_count_stddev FROM inner_cte ic JOIN SubnetDims sd ON sd.subnet_name = ic.subnet_name GROUP BY sd.ip_version, sd.dhcp_status WITH ROLLUP;

question: For load balancers that are ONLINE, list the provider name, load balancer ID, name, VIP address, and total connections. Do not repeat the provider name if it is the same as the previous row. Also include a subtotal row per provider showing the total number of ONLINE load balancers and the sum of total connections. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT lb.ID AS loadbalancer_id, lb.NAME AS loadbalancer_name, pra.PROVIDER_NAME AS provider_name, lb.VIP_ADDRESS AS vip_address, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY pra.PROVIDER_NAME ORDER BY stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS ) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb ON stats.LOADBALANCER_ID = lb.ID JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE lb.OPERATING_STATUS = 'ONLINE' ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(provider_name) OVER (ORDER BY provider_name_sort, provider_name, total_connections, loadbalancer_id) = provider_name THEN NULL ELSE provider_name END AS provider_name, loadbalancer_id, loadbalancer_name, vip_address, total_connections, total_online_loadbalancers FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.provider_name) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE i.provider_name END AS provider_name_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.provider_name) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE i.provider_name END AS provider_name, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.provider_name) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE i.loadbalancer_id END AS loadbalancer_id, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.provider_name) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE i.loadbalancer_name END AS loadbalancer_name, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.provider_name) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE i.vip_address END AS vip_address, SUM(i.window_column) AS total_connections, COUNT(i.loadbalancer_id) AS total_online_loadbalancers FROM inner_cte AS i GROUP BY i.provider_name, i.loadbalancer_id, i.loadbalancer_name, i.vip_address WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY provider_name_sort, provider_name, total_connections, loadbalancer_id;

question: For each RBAC action, show the action name, the average/range/variance of the referenced subnets’ IP version, include the overall average IP version across all RBAC-referenced subnets as a benchmark, and label each action as 'HIGH_IP_VERSION' (at least 10% above the benchmark), 'LOW_IP_VERSION' (at least 10% below), or 'AVERAGE_IP_VERSION'. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.ACTION AS rbac_action, AVG(s.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version, MAX(s.IP_VERSION) - MIN(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_range, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION IN (4, 6) GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_range DESC ), overall_benchmark AS ( SELECT AVG(s.IP_VERSION) AS benchmark_avg_ip_version FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION IN (4, 6) ) SELECT i.rbac_action, i.avg_ip_version, i.ip_version_range, i.ip_version_variance, b.benchmark_avg_ip_version AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.avg_ip_version > b.benchmark_avg_ip_version * 1.10 THEN 'HIGH_IP_VERSION' WHEN i.avg_ip_version < b.benchmark_avg_ip_version * 0.90 THEN 'LOW_IP_VERSION' ELSE 'AVERAGE_IP_VERSION' END AS ip_version_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN overall_benchmark b ORDER BY i.ip_version_range DESC;

question: For each port status, which statuses have a minimum admin_state_up value and an average standard_attr_id (considering only ports bound with VIF type 'ovs') such that their average standard_attr_id is greater than the overall average standard_attr_id across all 'ovs'-bound ports? Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) AS min_admin_state_up, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS avg_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE b.VIF_TYPE = 'ovs' GROUP BY p.STATUS) SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, inner_cte.min_admin_state_up, inner_cte.avg_standard_attr_id FROM inner_cte JOIN PORTS p ON p.STATUS = p.STATUS JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE b.VIF_TYPE = 'ovs' GROUP BY p.STATUS, inner_cte.min_admin_state_up, inner_cte.avg_standard_attr_id HAVING inner_cte.avg_standard_attr_id > ( SELECT AVG(p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) FROM PORTS p2 JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b2 ON p2.ID = b2.PORT_ID WHERE b2.VIF_TYPE = 'ovs' );

question: For each subnet name and its gateway IP, among subnets whose network has a RBAC action of 'access_as_shared' and whose subnet has DHCP enabled, find the maximum IP version; then, for each gateway IP, return the highest of those per-subnet maxima, keeping only gateway IPs where that highest value is greater than 3. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT s.name, MAX(s.ip_version) AS max_ip_version, s.gateway_ip FROM NETWORKRBACS n JOIN SUBNETS s ON n.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.action = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY s.name, s.gateway_ip HAVING MAX(s.ip_version) > 3) SELECT inner_cte.gateway_ip, MAX(inner_cte.max_ip_version) AS max_ip_version_across_subnets FROM inner_cte JOIN SUBNETS s2 ON s2.name = inner_cte.name AND s2.gateway_ip = inner_cte.gateway_ip WHERE s2.enable_dhcp = 1 GROUP BY inner_cte.gateway_ip HAVING MAX(inner_cte.max_ip_version) > 3;

question: For load balancers provided by “haproxy”, list only those whose total connections are greater than the average total connections across all “haproxy” load balancers, and return the load balancer name, VIP address, bytes in, total connections, and the same row number ordered by load balancer name using a window frame of 2 preceding and 1 following rows. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT lb.NAME AS loadbalancer_name, lb.VIP_ADDRESS AS vip_address, stats.BYTES_IN AS bytes_in, stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS AS total_connections, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY lb.NAME ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb ON stats.LOADBALANCER_ID = lb.ID JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' ), ProviderAverages AS ( SELECT pra.PROVIDER_NAME, AVG(stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS) AS avg_total_connections FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb ON stats.LOADBALANCER_ID = lb.ID JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID GROUP BY pra.PROVIDER_NAME ) SELECT i.loadbalancer_name, i.vip_address, i.bytes_in, i.total_connections, i.window_column FROM inner_cte i JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS lb2 ON lb2.NAME = i.loadbalancer_name AND lb2.VIP_ADDRESS = i.vip_address JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS pra2 ON lb2.ID = pra2.RESOURCE_ID WHERE i.total_connections > ( SELECT avg_total_connections FROM ProviderAverages WHERE ProviderAverages.PROVIDER_NAME = pra2.PROVIDER_NAME ) ORDER BY i.loadbalancer_name;

question: For each security group, find the security group ID and the highest rank (when ordering DOWN ports by port ID within that security group) among all DOWN ports bound to that security group. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN') SELECT security_group_id, MAX(window_column) AS max_port_rank FROM inner_cte GROUP BY security_group_id;

question: For the top 10 port statuses with the highest coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of ports’ standard attribute IDs (considering only ports that have both a security group port binding and a port security binding), show the port status, the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP), and whether any of those ports have a floating IP allocated. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ) SELECT i.status, i.coefficient_of_variation, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT f.id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_floating_ips FROM inner_cte i JOIN ports p ON p.status = i.status JOIN securitygroupportbindings sgpb ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN floatingips f ON f.fixed_port_id = p.id GROUP BY i.status, i.coefficient_of_variation ORDER BY i.coefficient_of_variation DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For networks that are marked as default external networks (IS_DEFAULT = 0), return only those networks whose computed dense rank (ordered by the RBAC action, using a window frame of the current row and the 2 preceding rows) is greater than the average dense rank across all such networks; list the network name and its dense rank. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY r.ACTION ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.ID = r.OBJECT_ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0) SELECT NAME, window_column FROM inner_cte WHERE window_column > (SELECT AVG(window_column) FROM inner_cte);

question: Among the top 10 subnets (by the largest range of allocation-pool starting IPs) for routes whose next hop is 10.30.19.197/8, show each subnet’s name, the computed FIRST_IP range and variance, and whether the subnet has any allocation pool whose LAST_IP equals the subnet’s GATEWAY_IP. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(p.FIRST_IP) - MIN(p.FIRST_IP) AS first_ip_range, VARIANCE(p.FIRST_IP) AS first_ip_variance FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE r.NEXTHOP = '10.30.19.197/8' GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY first_ip_range DESC ) SELECT i.subnet_name, i.first_ip_range, i.first_ip_variance, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT p2.ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_pool_ending_at_gateway FROM inner_cte i JOIN SUBNETS s2 ON s2.NAME = i.subnet_name LEFT JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p2 ON p2.SUBNET_ID = s2.ID AND p2.LAST_IP = s2.GATEWAY_IP GROUP BY i.subnet_name, i.first_ip_range, i.first_ip_variance ORDER BY i.first_ip_range DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For each network status, show the status and compute both the variance and the standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the security group binding order (PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) across networks that have at least one security binding, considering only network statuses that have at least 3 distinct networks with security bindings. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.STATUS AS network_status, VARIANCE(nsb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) AS port_security_enabled_variance, STDDEV(nsb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) AS port_security_enabled_stddev FROM NETWORKS AS n JOIN NETWORKSECURITYBINDINGS AS nsb ON n.ID = nsb.NETWORK_ID GROUP BY n.STATUS ORDER BY port_security_enabled_variance DESC) SELECT i.network_status, i.port_security_enabled_variance, i.port_security_enabled_stddev FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN NETWORKS AS n ON n.STATUS = i.network_status JOIN NETWORKSECURITYBINDINGS AS nsb ON n.ID = nsb.NETWORK_ID GROUP BY i.network_status, i.port_security_enabled_variance, i.port_security_enabled_stddev HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT n.ID) >= 3 ORDER BY i.port_security_enabled_variance DESC;

question: For ports that are DOWN, show the port name, MAC address, admin_state_up flag, binding host, VIF type, and the average admin_state_up in a window of 2 preceding and 2 following rows partitioned by VIF type and ordered by MAC address; additionally, for each VIF type, include the total number of DOWN ports, the overall average of those per-VIF-type totals as a benchmark, and categorize each VIF type as 'HIGH_DOWN' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_DOWN' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_DOWN'. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), VifDownCounts AS ( SELECT VIF_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS total_down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY VIF_TYPE ), AverageDownCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(total_down_ports) AS avg_down_ports FROM VifDownCounts ) SELECT i.NAME, i.MAC_ADDRESS, i.ADMIN_STATE_UP, i.HOST, i.VIF_TYPE, i.window_column, vdc.total_down_ports, adc.avg_down_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN vdc.total_down_ports > adc.avg_down_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_DOWN' WHEN vdc.total_down_ports < adc.avg_down_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_DOWN' ELSE 'AVERAGE_DOWN' END AS down_category FROM inner_cte i JOIN VifDownCounts vdc ON i.VIF_TYPE = vdc.VIF_TYPE CROSS JOIN AverageDownCounts adc ORDER BY i.MAC_ADDRESS;

question: For each administratively up port that has at least one IP allocation, list the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the number of IP allocations on that port, the number of subnet-id rows among those allocations, and the deviation of that port’s IP allocation count from the average IP allocation count across all such ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ia.subnet_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS subnet_id_rows FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(ip_allocation_count) AS avg_ip_allocation_count FROM inner_cte ) SELECT ic.port_id, ic.tenant_id, ic.mac_address, ic.ip_allocation_count, ic.subnet_id_rows, (ic.ip_allocation_count - a.avg_ip_allocation_count) AS deviation_from_avg_ip_allocations FROM inner_cte ic CROSS JOIN avg_cte a;

question: For each tenant that has ports in DOWN status, list the tenant ID, the number of DOWN ports, the average number of DOWN ports across all such tenants as a benchmark, and categorize each tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), TenantDownPorts AS (SELECT p.tenant_id, COUNT(p.id) AS total_down_ports FROM PORTS AS p JOIN inner_cte AS ic ON ic.MAC_ADDRESS = p.MAC_ADDRESS GROUP BY p.tenant_id), AverageDownPorts AS (SELECT AVG(total_down_ports) AS avg_down_ports FROM TenantDownPorts) SELECT tdp.tenant_id, tdp.total_down_ports, adp.avg_down_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tdp.total_down_ports > adp.avg_down_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tdp.total_down_ports < adp.avg_down_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM TenantDownPorts AS tdp CROSS JOIN AverageDownPorts AS adp;

question: For networks that are marked as default external networks (IS_DEFAULT = 0), list each network name and its dense rank when ordered by the RBAC action (using a window frame of the current row and the 2 preceding rows), along with the total number of such networks and the average number of such networks per RBAC action. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY r.ACTION ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.ID = r.OBJECT_ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0 ) SELECT inner_cte.NAME, inner_cte.window_column, COUNT(*) AS total_networks, avg_counts.avg_networks_per_action FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(action_count) AS avg_networks_per_action FROM ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS action_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY window_column ) AS sub ) AS avg_counts ON 1 = 1 GROUP BY inner_cte.NAME, inner_cte.window_column, avg_counts.avg_networks_per_action;

question: For ports with status equal to 'DOWN', show the port ID, port name, MAC address, the allocated IP address, subnet ID, and the average port ID within each port ID group ordered by IP address; additionally, group the results by port status and subnet ID to list the number of distinct ports, including subtotals per status and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ia.SUBNET_ID AS subnet_id, AVG(p.ID) OVER (PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS), PortSubnetCounts AS ( SELECT 'DOWN' AS status, inner_cte.subnet_id, COUNT(DISTINCT inner_cte.port_id) AS total_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY inner_cte.subnet_id ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(status) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE status END AS status, CASE WHEN GROUPING(subnet_id) = 1 AND GROUPING(status) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE subnet_id END AS subnet_id, SUM(total_ports) AS total_ports FROM PortSubnetCounts GROUP BY status, subnet_id WITH ROLLUP;

question: For each load balancer operating status, list the operating status and total number of “haproxy” load balancers, but only include operating statuses where that count represents more than 50% of all “haproxy” load balancers. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT lb.OPERATING_STATUS, COUNT(*) AS total_loadbalancers FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' GROUP BY lb.OPERATING_STATUS HAVING COUNT(*) > 1) SELECT i.OPERATING_STATUS, i.total_loadbalancers FROM inner_cte i JOIN ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_haproxy_loadbalancers FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb2 JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra2 ON lb2.ID = pra2.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra2.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' ) totals ON 1 = 1 WHERE (i.total_loadbalancers * 1.0 / totals.total_haproxy_loadbalancers) > 0.50;

question: For each port status and device owner, considering only ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports', return the port status, device owner, and the maximum number of ports found in any single network for that status/owner combination. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER), NetworkPortCounts AS (SELECT p.network_id, p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS ports_in_network FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.network_id, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER) SELECT npc.port_status, npc.device_owner, MAX(npc.ports_in_network) AS max_ports_in_any_network FROM NetworkPortCounts npc JOIN inner_cte ic ON ic.port_status = npc.port_status AND ic.device_owner = npc.device_owner GROUP BY npc.port_status, npc.device_owner;

question: For each tenant that has at least one port bound to a security group with admin_state_up = 1, list the tenant ID, the total number of such ports they have, the total number of security group bindings across those ports, the total number of DNS records across those ports, and the average number of such ports per tenant. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name) SELECT inner_cte.tenant_id, COUNT(inner_cte.port_id) AS total_ports_with_sg_binding_admin_up, SUM(inner_cte.security_group_binding_count) AS total_security_group_bindings, SUM(inner_cte.dns_record_count) AS total_dns_records, avg_ports.avg_port_count AS avg_ports_with_sg_binding_admin_up_per_tenant FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count FROM ( SELECT COUNT(port_id) AS port_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS sub ) AS avg_ports GROUP BY inner_cte.tenant_id, avg_ports.avg_port_count;

question: For ports that are bound to the security group ID 0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c, show the port ID, port status, allocated IP address, and the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within each network ordered by standard attribute ID. Do not repeat the network ID if it is the same as the previous row, and include a subtotal row per network showing the number of ports and the maximum running-sum value. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.STATUS AS port_status, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(network_id) OVER (ORDER BY network_id_sort, network_id, port_id) = network_id THEN NULL ELSE network_id END AS network_id, port_id, port_status, ip_address, window_column, total_ports, max_window_column FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(p.NETWORK_ID) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE p.NETWORK_ID END AS network_id_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(p.NETWORK_ID) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE p.NETWORK_ID END AS network_id, i.port_id, i.port_status, i.ip_address, i.window_column, COUNT(DISTINCT i.port_id) AS total_ports, MAX(i.window_column) AS max_window_column FROM inner_cte i JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = i.port_id GROUP BY p.NETWORK_ID, i.port_id, i.port_status, i.ip_address, i.window_column WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY network_id_sort, network_id, port_id;

question: From the top 10 VIF types with the highest number of DOWN ports, display each VIF type, total number of DOWN ports, and the average of the per-port windowed admin_state_up (computed over 2 preceding and 2 following rows partitioned by VIF type and ordered by MAC address). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ) SELECT i.VIF_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS total_down_ports, AVG(i.window_column) AS avg_window_admin_state_up FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b2 ON i.MAC_ADDRESS IS NOT NULL AND i.VIF_TYPE = b2.VIF_TYPE GROUP BY i.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY total_down_ports DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For IPv4 subnets, list each subnet name, the dense rank of its associated standard attribute ID when ordered by the standard attribute’s updated-at timestamp (using a window frame of the current row and the 2 preceding rows), the overall average of these dense ranks across all IPv4 subnets as a benchmark, and categorize each subnet as 'HIGH_RANK' (at least 50% above average), 'LOW_RANK' (at least 50% below average), or 'AVERAGE_RANK'. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY sa.UPDATED_AT ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES AS sa ON sa.ID = s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ), avg_rank AS ( SELECT AVG(window_column) AS avg_window_column FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.NAME, i.window_column, a.avg_window_column AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.window_column > a.avg_window_column * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_RANK' WHEN i.window_column < a.avg_window_column * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_RANK' ELSE 'AVERAGE_RANK' END AS rank_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_rank a;

question: Among the load balancers associated with the provider named 'haproxy' whose highest admin_state_up value is 1, list the top 10 tenants by number of such load balancers, showing each tenant ID, the total number of qualifying load balancers, and whether any of those load balancers are currently operating ONLINE. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT lb.name AS loadbalancer_name, MAX(lb.admin_state_up) AS max_admin_state_up, lb.operating_status FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS lb JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS pra ON lb.id = pra.resource_id WHERE pra.provider_name = 'haproxy' GROUP BY lb.name, lb.operating_status HAVING MAX(lb.admin_state_up) = 1 ) SELECT lb.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT lb.id) AS total_qualifying_loadbalancers, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN inner_cte.operating_status = 'ONLINE' THEN lb.id END) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_any_online FROM inner_cte JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS lb ON lb.name = inner_cte.loadbalancer_name AND lb.operating_status = inner_cte.operating_status GROUP BY lb.tenant_id ORDER BY total_qualifying_loadbalancers DESC LIMIT 10;

question: Among the top 3 networks that have the most subnets (considering only RBAC entries where the action is 'access_as_shared'), list each network object ID and its subnet count, and also show the tenant ID of each subnet on those networks. Do not repeat the network ID if it is the same as the previous row. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.OBJECT_ID AS network_id, COUNT(*) AS subnet_count FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.OBJECT_ID ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 3 ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(inner_cte.network_id) OVER (ORDER BY inner_cte.network_id) = inner_cte.network_id THEN NULL ELSE inner_cte.network_id END AS network_id, inner_cte.subnet_count, s.TENANT_ID AS subnet_tenant_id FROM inner_cte JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON s.NETWORK_ID = inner_cte.network_id ORDER BY inner_cte.network_id, s.TENANT_ID;

question: For each tenant, how many ports are in status 'DOWN' with port security enabled, and what is the deviation of that count from the average across all tenants? Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1), TenantDownSecurePorts AS (SELECT p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS down_secure_ports FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 GROUP BY p.TENANT_ID), AverageTenantCounts AS (SELECT AVG(down_secure_ports) AS avg_down_secure_ports FROM TenantDownSecurePorts) SELECT tdsp.tenant_id, tdsp.down_secure_ports, (tdsp.down_secure_ports - atc.avg_down_secure_ports) AS deviation_from_avg, inner_cte.down_ports_with_port_security_enabled AS total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM TenantDownSecurePorts tdsp CROSS JOIN AverageTenantCounts atc CROSS JOIN inner_cte;

question: For each security group, show the security group ID, the range/variance/standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the number of allowed address pairs per port (only counting ports that have at least one allowed address pair), also show the overall average of the security-group-level range as a benchmark, and categorize each security group as 'HIGH_SPREAD' (at least 50% above the benchmark), 'LOW_SPREAD' (at least 50% below the benchmark), or 'AVERAGE_SPREAD'. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MAX(port_pair_count) - MIN(port_pair_count) AS pair_count_range, VARIANCE(port_pair_count) AS pair_count_variance, STDDEV(port_pair_count) AS pair_count_stddev FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS port_pair_count FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ALLOWEDADDRESSPAIRS AS aap ON p.ID = aap.PORT_ID GROUP BY p.ID ) AS port_stats ON sgpb.PORT_ID = port_stats.port_id GROUP BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY pair_count_range DESC ), AverageRange AS ( SELECT AVG(pair_count_range) AS avg_pair_count_range FROM inner_cte ) SELECT ic.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, ic.pair_count_range, ic.pair_count_variance, ic.pair_count_stddev, ar.avg_pair_count_range AS benchmark, CASE WHEN ic.pair_count_range > ar.avg_pair_count_range * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_SPREAD' WHEN ic.pair_count_range < ar.avg_pair_count_range * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_SPREAD' ELSE 'AVERAGE_SPREAD' END AS spread_category FROM inner_cte ic CROSS JOIN AverageRange ar;

question: For each port status, report the minimum admin_state_up value and the average standard_attr_id for ports bound with VIF type 'ovs', and also show how each status’s average standard_attr_id deviates from the overall average standard_attr_id across all such ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) AS min_admin_state_up, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS avg_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE b.VIF_TYPE = 'ovs' GROUP BY p.STATUS ), overall_avg AS ( SELECT AVG(avg_standard_attr_id) AS overall_avg_standard_attr_id FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.min_admin_state_up, i.avg_standard_attr_id, (i.avg_standard_attr_id - o.overall_avg_standard_attr_id) AS deviation_from_overall_avg_standard_attr_id FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN overall_avg o;

question: For each IPv4 subnet route, show the destination, next hop, subnet name and CIDR, and the allocation pool’s first and last IP (including the dense rank within each subnet as before). Also include, for each subnet, how many routes it has and the deviation of that subnet’s route count from the average route count across all IPv4 subnets. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT r.DESTINATION, r.NEXTHOP, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.SUBNET_ID ORDER BY r.SUBNET_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4), SubnetRouteCounts AS ( SELECT s.id AS subnet_id, COUNT(r.destination) AS route_count FROM subnets s LEFT JOIN subnetroutes r ON r.subnet_id = s.id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.id ), AverageRouteCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(route_count) AS avg_route_count FROM SubnetRouteCounts ) SELECT ic.DESTINATION, ic.NEXTHOP, ic.subnet_name, ic.subnet_cidr, ic.FIRST_IP, ic.LAST_IP, ic.window_column, src.route_count, (src.route_count - arc.avg_route_count) AS deviation_from_avg_route_count FROM inner_cte ic JOIN subnets s ON s.cidr = ic.subnet_cidr AND s.name = ic.subnet_name JOIN SubnetRouteCounts src ON src.subnet_id = s.id CROSS JOIN AverageRouteCounts arc;

question: Using the allowed address pairs on the port with ID `25d421c1-c76d-4c26-9550-9f871a1d5034`, return the allowed address pair MAC address, allowed address pair IP address, the port ID, the security group ID bound to that port, and the running average of the port’s standard attribute ID within each port (partitioned by port ID) ordered by the allowed address pair IP address. Also include the port’s tenant ID, the total number of ports owned by that tenant, the average number of ports across all tenants as a benchmark, and classify the tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT aap.MAC_ADDRESS AS allowed_mac_address, aap.IP_ADDRESS AS allowed_ip_address, p.ID AS port_id, sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS security_group_id, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY aap.IP_ADDRESS ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN ALLOWEDADDRESSPAIRS AS aap ON p.ID = aap.PORT_ID WHERE p.ID = '25d421c1-c76d-4c26-9550-9f871a1d5034' ORDER BY aap.IP_ADDRESS ), TenantPorts AS ( SELECT p2.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, COUNT(p2.ID) AS total_ports FROM PORTS AS p2 GROUP BY p2.TENANT_ID ), AveragePorts AS ( SELECT AVG(total_ports) AS avg_ports FROM TenantPorts ) SELECT i.allowed_mac_address, i.allowed_ip_address, i.port_id, i.security_group_id, i.window_column, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, tp.total_ports, ap.avg_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tp.total_ports > ap.avg_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tp.total_ports < ap.avg_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN PORTS AS p ON p.ID = i.port_id JOIN TenantPorts AS tp ON tp.tenant_id = p.TENANT_ID CROSS JOIN AveragePorts AS ap ORDER BY i.allowed_ip_address;

question: For subnets whose network has a RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', show the IP version, a label indicating whether the subnet has DHCP enabled ('DHCP' if enabled, 'No DHCP' otherwise), and the number of matching subnets. Include subtotals per IP version and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ), SubnetSummary AS ( SELECT s.IP_VERSION AS ip_version, CASE WHEN s.ENABLE_DHCP = 1 THEN 'DHCP' ELSE 'No DHCP' END AS dhcp_status, COUNT(*) AS total_subnets FROM inner_cte i JOIN SUBNETS s ON s.NAME = i.subnet_name AND s.CIDR = i.subnet_cidr GROUP BY s.IP_VERSION, dhcp_status ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(ip_version) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE CAST(ip_version AS CHAR) END AS ip_version, CASE WHEN GROUPING(dhcp_status) = 1 AND GROUPING(ip_version) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE dhcp_status END AS dhcp_status, SUM(total_subnets) AS total_subnets FROM SubnetSummary GROUP BY ip_version, dhcp_status WITH ROLLUP;

question: For allowed address pairs on the port with ID `25d421c1-c76d-4c26-9550-9f871a1d5034`, show the allowed address pair MAC address, allowed address pair IP address, the port ID, the security group ID bound to that port, and the running average of the port’s standard attribute ID within each port (partitioned by port ID) ordered by the allowed address pair IP address, along with the total number of security group bindings on that port and the average number of security group bindings per port across all ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT aap.MAC_ADDRESS AS allowed_mac_address, aap.IP_ADDRESS AS allowed_ip_address, p.ID AS port_id, sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS security_group_id, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY aap.IP_ADDRESS ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN ALLOWEDADDRESSPAIRS AS aap ON p.ID = aap.PORT_ID WHERE p.ID = '25d421c1-c76d-4c26-9550-9f871a1d5034' ORDER BY aap.IP_ADDRESS ) SELECT inner_cte.allowed_mac_address, inner_cte.allowed_ip_address, inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.security_group_id, inner_cte.window_column, port_sg_counts.total_sg_bindings_on_port, avg_sg.avg_sg_bindings_per_port FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT sgpb.PORT_ID AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS total_sg_bindings_on_port FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb GROUP BY sgpb.PORT_ID ) AS port_sg_counts ON port_sg_counts.port_id = inner_cte.port_id JOIN ( SELECT AVG(sg_count) AS avg_sg_bindings_per_port FROM ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS sg_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS GROUP BY PORT_ID ) AS sub ) AS avg_sg ON 1 = 1 ORDER BY inner_cte.allowed_ip_address;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, list the port ID, tenant ID, and MAC address, along with the running sum of standard attribute IDs within each resource type group ordered by standard attribute ID; only include ports whose standard attribute ID is greater than the average standard attribute ID among DOWN ports for the same resource type. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), ResourceTypeAverages AS (SELECT sa.RESOURCE_TYPE, AVG(sa.ID) AS avg_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.window_column FROM inner_cte i JOIN PORTS p2 ON p2.ID = i.port_id JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa2 ON sa2.ID = p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa2.ID > (SELECT avg_standard_attr_id FROM ResourceTypeAverages rta WHERE rta.RESOURCE_TYPE = sa2.RESOURCE_TYPE);

question: For load balancers provided by “haproxy”, list only those whose bytes in are above the average bytes in across all “haproxy” load balancers; return the load balancer name, VIP address, bytes in, total connections, and the same row number window (ordered by load balancer name with a frame of 2 preceding and 1 following rows). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT lb.NAME AS loadbalancer_name, lb.VIP_ADDRESS AS vip_address, stats.BYTES_IN AS bytes_in, stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS AS total_connections, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY lb.NAME ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb ON stats.LOADBALANCER_ID = lb.ID JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' ), haproxy_avg AS ( SELECT AVG(stats2.BYTES_IN * 1.0) AS avg_bytes_in FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats2 JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb2 ON stats2.LOADBALANCER_ID = lb2.ID JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra2 ON lb2.ID = pra2.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra2.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' ) SELECT i.loadbalancer_name, i.vip_address, i.bytes_in, i.total_connections, i.window_column FROM inner_cte AS i CROSS JOIN haproxy_avg AS a WHERE i.bytes_in > a.avg_bytes_in ORDER BY i.loadbalancer_name;

question: Using the allowed address pairs on the port with ID `25d421c1-c76d-4c26-9550-9f871a1d5034`, list the allowed address pair MAC address, allowed address pair IP address, port ID, security group ID bound to that port, and the running average of the port’s standard attribute ID within each port (partitioned by port ID) ordered by the allowed address pair IP address; then return only those rows where the running average is greater than 0. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT aap.MAC_ADDRESS AS allowed_mac_address, aap.IP_ADDRESS AS allowed_ip_address, p.ID AS port_id, sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS security_group_id, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY aap.IP_ADDRESS ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN ALLOWEDADDRESSPAIRS AS aap ON p.ID = aap.PORT_ID WHERE p.ID = '25d421c1-c76d-4c26-9550-9f871a1d5034' ORDER BY aap.IP_ADDRESS) SELECT allowed_mac_address, allowed_ip_address, port_id, security_group_id, window_column FROM inner_cte WHERE window_column > 0 ORDER BY allowed_ip_address;

question: For each load balancer operating status, show the operating status, the total number of load balancers associated with the “haproxy” provider (only keeping statuses where this count is greater than 1), the average of these per-status totals as a benchmark, and categorize each status as 'HIGH_COUNT' (at least 50% above average), 'LOW_COUNT' (at least 50% below average), or 'AVERAGE_COUNT'. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT lb.OPERATING_STATUS, COUNT(*) AS total_loadbalancers FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' GROUP BY lb.OPERATING_STATUS HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(total_loadbalancers) AS avg_loadbalancers FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.OPERATING_STATUS, i.total_loadbalancers, a.avg_loadbalancers AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.total_loadbalancers > a.avg_loadbalancers * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_COUNT' WHEN i.total_loadbalancers < a.avg_loadbalancers * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_COUNT' ELSE 'AVERAGE_COUNT' END AS count_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a;

question: For each ACTIVE network, show the network name, its total number of security bindings, the average number of security bindings across all ACTIVE networks as a benchmark, and categorize the network as 'HIGH_BINDINGS' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_BINDINGS' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_BINDINGS'. Only include networks that have more than 1 security binding. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.name AS network_name, SUM(1) AS total_security_bindings FROM NETWORKS n JOIN NETWORKSECURITYBINDINGS nsb ON n.id = nsb.network_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n.name HAVING SUM(1) > 1), AverageBindings AS ( SELECT AVG(total_security_bindings) AS avg_bindings FROM inner_cte ) SELECT ic.network_name, ic.total_security_bindings, ab.avg_bindings AS benchmark, CASE WHEN ic.total_security_bindings > ab.avg_bindings * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_BINDINGS' WHEN ic.total_security_bindings < ab.avg_bindings * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_BINDINGS' ELSE 'AVERAGE_BINDINGS' END AS bindings_category FROM inner_cte ic CROSS JOIN AverageBindings ab;

question: For each subnet name and its gateway IP, find the maximum IP version among subnets whose network has a RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', keep only groups where that maximum IP version is greater than 3, and also report how many such subnet name/gateway IP groups exist in total along with each group’s deviation from that overall average maximum IP version. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT s.name, MAX(s.ip_version) AS max_ip_version, s.gateway_ip FROM NETWORKRBACS n JOIN SUBNETS s ON n.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.action = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY s.name, s.gateway_ip HAVING MAX(s.ip_version) > 3), avg_cte AS (SELECT AVG(max_ip_version) AS avg_max_ip_version, COUNT(*) AS total_groups FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.name, i.gateway_ip, i.max_ip_version, a.total_groups, (i.max_ip_version - a.avg_max_ip_version) AS deviation_from_avg_max_ip_version FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a;

question: For each port status and device owner, considering only ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports', list the port status, device owner, number of ports, and earliest standard attribute updated timestamp, but only include groups where at least 80% of the ports have ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), AdminUpUtilization AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, SUM(CASE WHEN p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS admin_up_ports, COUNT(p.ID) AS total_ports FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.earliest_standard_attr_update FROM inner_cte i JOIN AdminUpUtilization a ON a.port_status = i.port_status AND a.device_owner = i.device_owner WHERE a.total_ports > 0 AND (a.admin_up_ports * 1.0 / a.total_ports) >= 0.80;
